title: Personalized: Customer Strategy in the Age of AI / BCG Personalization Index
author_source: Mark Abraham, David Edelman; Boston Consulting Group (book with HBR Press, Oct 2024) and BCG Personalization Index articles
note: BCG claims USD 2 trillion in revenue will shift to firms that personalise experiences; based on a survey of 5,000 customers in 10 countries and 100 executive interviews; Personalization Index for retailers (USD 570 bn incremental growth via first-party data). Shows how AI moves targeting from segments to individuals.
course_use: Discussion input; articles free, book paid (approx. EUR 30).

title: The Elements of Value
author_source: Eric Almquist, John Senior, Nicolas Bloch; Bain & Company / Harvard Business Review, Sept 2016
note: 30 consumer value elements in four layers (functional, emotional, life changing, social impact) in a Maslow-style pyramid, with interactive graphic; evidence that brands delivering more elements earn higher loyalty and growth. A needs-based segmentation and value-proposition/positioning checklist.
course_use: In-class exercise: map two competing brands on the pyramid to find a positioning gap; Bain page free, full HBR article via WU-Lizenz prüfen (HBR/EBSCO).

title: The B2B Elements of Value
author_source: Eric Almquist, Jamie Cleghorn, Lori Sherer; Bain & Company / Harvard Business Review, March-April 2018
note: 40 B2B value elements in five tiers (table stakes, functional, ease of doing business, individual, inspirational); basis for needs-based B2B segmentation and differentiated value propositions for buying-centre roles.
course_use: B2B positioning exercise; Bain summary free, HBR article via WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Embrace meaningful personalization to maximize growth (Personalizing growth)
author_source: Deloitte Digital; research report, c. 2024
note: Consultancy view on personalisation maturity (maturity curve), linking customer data, segmentation and experience personalisation to growth and loyalty; shows how firms operationalise targeting.
course_use: Optional practitioner reading; free (registration may be required).

title: Gartner Survey Reveals Personalization Can Triple the Likelihood of Customer Regret at Key Journey Points
author_source: Gartner Inc. (Audrey Brosnan); press release, 3 June 2025; survey of 1,464 B2B buyers and consumers (North America, UK, Australia/NZ)
note: Counter-evidence to personalisation hype: 53% had negative experiences with personalised marketing; they were 3.2x more likely to regret a purchase and 44% less likely to buy again, though 1.8x more willing to pay a premium. Balances the McKinsey/BCG view.
course_use: Pair with McKinsey 2021 for a pro/contra debate; press release free, full Gartner research paid.

title: Media in Focus: Marketing Effectiveness in the Digital Era
author_source: Les Binet, Peter Field; IPA with Google and Thinkbox, Oct 2017; meta-analysis of the IPA Effectiveness Databank
note: Explicitly tests whether tight targeting is now the most efficient approach: broad reach and mass marketing still drive long-term growth, narrow targeting suits short-term activation; warns against short-termism. Core evidence for 'how narrowly should we target?'.
course_use: Key reading for the targeting session; free PDF via Thinkbox, print via IPA.

title: Effectiveness in Context: A Manual for Brand Building
author_source: Les Binet, Peter Field; IPA, 2018; report based on the IPA Effectiveness Databank
note: Shows how the optimal brand/activation balance, reach and targeting depend on context (category, brand size, growth stage, B2B vs. B2C, online vs. offline brands); qualifies one-size rules such as 60:40.
course_use: Advanced reading for master students; IPA purchase/members, summaries and charts free.

title: The 95-5 Rule and B2B research on future buyers (LinkedIn B2B Institute with Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)
author_source: John Dawes (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute) for the LinkedIn B2B Institute, 2021; research series incl. 'The Double Jeopardy Law in B2B' (Romaniuk, Dawes & Faghidno, 2021)
note: Evidence that only about 5% of B2B buyers are in-market per quarter, so targeting only in-market intent signals misses the 95% of future buyers; Double Jeopardy also holds in B2B. Strong input for B2B targeting debates (brand building vs. account-based/intent targeting).
course_use: Free reports in the B2B Institute library; use in a B2B targeting session.

title: Kantar BrandZ Most Valuable Global Brands 2025
author_source: Kantar; annual report, May 2025 (20th edition); brand valuation study (approx. 4.5 m interviews, 22k brands, 54 markets)
note: Brand contribution modelled via 'Meaningful, Different, Salient', linking meaningful difference (positioning) to brand value; Global Top 100 worth USD 10.7 tn; cases such as Apple, NVIDIA and newcomer ChatGPT.
course_use: Use MDS framework and ranking data for positioning case discussions; free download (registration).

title: Sinus-Milieus Österreich (update 2022, 'Vorwärts in die Vergangenheit')
author_source: INTEGRAL Markt- und Meinungsforschung (Vienna) with SINUS-Institut Heidelberg; full model update Oct 2022 (survey of 1,000 Austrians aged 16-75; first Austrian model 2001); commercial segmentation model
note: Austria's leading values/lifestyle segmentation: ten milieus positioned by social status and basic values - Conservative-Established 11%, Post-Materialists 11%, Performers 9%, Cosmopolitan Individualists 6%, Progressive Realists 7%, Adaptive-Pragmatic Middle 14%, Nostalgic Middle 12%, Traditionals 10%, Consumption-Oriented 9%, Hedonists 11%. The milieu map is ideal for teaching psychographic segmentation in a local context.
course_use: Show the milieu map; students assign Austrian brands to target milieus; overview free, detailed data paid via INTEGRAL (possible guest speaker).

title: Sinus-Milieus Deutschland
author_source: SINUS-Institut Heidelberg; commercial segmentation model (10 milieus, updated regularly)
note: German milieu model on the two dimensions social status and value orientation, with short milieu profiles and shares; widely used in media planning; compare with the Austrian model and with VALS.
course_use: Comparative exercise Austria vs. Germany vs. US (VALS); overview free, data paid.

title: Beyond Red vs. Blue: The Political Typology (2026)
author_source: Pew Research Center; report, 10 June 2026; survey of 10,357 US adults (Nov 2025), cluster analysis; previous edition Nov 2021 (10,221 adults, nine groups)
note: Fully documented non-commercial segmentation: nine groups built by cluster analysis on values, not party (e.g., Leftward Progressives 7%, Order and Opportunity Left 18%, Tuned-Out Middle 9%, Faith First Conservatives 12%, No Apologies Right 9%); methodology appendix and an online quiz that classifies respondents into segments. Comparing 2021 and 2026 groups shows segment change over time.
course_use: Students take the quiz, then discuss segmentation bases, cluster solution and profiling; free (report, PDF, quiz).

title: Claritas PRIZM Premier segmentation (MyBestSegments)
author_source: Claritas; commercial geodemographic segmentation system (US), 68 segments in 11 lifestage and 14 social groups
note: Classic geodemographic segmentation: ZIP-code look-up shows top segments per area with demographic/lifestyle snapshots and segment profiles; demonstrates how segments become addressable via location.
course_use: In-class demo with well-known US ZIP codes; free look-up, full data paid.

title: Experian Mosaic (UK) household and postcode segmentation
author_source: Experian; commercial geodemographic classification; UK: 15 groups and 66 types (440+ data elements); Germany: 10 groups and 41 types
note: Leading European geodemographic system; free local-authority Mosaic profiles (e.g., Tower Hamlets, Sefton) show how segments are profiled and used for public-service targeting; compare with PRIZM and Sinus.
course_use: Use a free council Mosaic profile PDF as a profiling example; product data paid.

title: VALS (Values and Lifestyles) framework and survey
author_source: Strategic Business Insights (spin-off of SRI International); US psychographic segmentation system, eight segments
note: Eight US consumer segments on two dimensions - primary motivation (ideals, achievement, self-expression) and resources (from Innovators to Survivors); free online survey classifies respondents. Standard psychographic example in Kotler and consumer behaviour texts.
course_use: Students take the free VALS survey and reflect on fit; free survey, commercial data paid.

title: Why Consumer Intent Is More Powerful Than Demographics
author_source: Lisa Gevelber; Think with Google, Dec 2015; industry article/white paper (PDF)
note: Argues demographic targeting can miss over 70% of potential mobile shoppers (e.g., 56% of sporting-goods searchers are women; 40% of baby-product buyers live in households without children): 'intent beats identity'. Google's own data with commercial interest - good for critical evaluation of segmentation bases.
course_use: Discussion piece on demographic vs. behavioural/intent segmentation; free.

title: Verbrauchsausgaben - Hauptergebnisse der Konsumerhebung 2019/2020
author_source: Statistik Austria; official statistics report, June 2021 (five-yearly survey, 7,139 households)
note: Austrian household spending by category, household type, income, age and region (avg. EUR 3,250/month; housing/energy 24.4%, transport 13.9%, leisure 13.4%, food 12.1%); ideal for sizing and evaluating Austrian segments in student projects. Check for results of the 2024/25 round.
course_use: Data source for segment size/attractiveness calculations; free (PDF, STATcube tables).

title: Household budget survey - statistics on consumption expenditure (Statistics Explained)
author_source: Eurostat; official statistics article, 2020 HBS round (26 EU countries)
note: EU consumption structure (housing 32.9%, food 16.9%, transport 10.9%) and spending by income quintile (top 20% spend more than twice the bottom 20% per person in half of EU countries); datasets hbs_exp_t133 (income quintile) and hbs_exp_t135 (age of reference person) for cross-country segment comparisons.
course_use: Data for international segmentation/targeting exercises; free.

title: ICC/ESOMAR International Code on Market, Opinion and Social Research and Data Analytics
author_source: ICC and ESOMAR; code of conduct, revised Dec 2016 (newer edition c. 2025), plus ESOMAR Data Protection Checklist
note: Ethics and data-protection rules for data used in segmentation and targeting: data minimisation (Art. 3), secondary data use (Art. 5), data protection and privacy (Art. 6); scope extended to data analytics in 2016. Frames responsible profiling and targeting.
course_use: Short reading for the ethics of segmentation/targeting; free PDF.

title: IAB Europe Guide to the Post Third-Party Cookie Era (updated March 2022)
author_source: IAB Europe Programmatic Trading Committee; industry guide (1st ed. May 2020, 2nd Feb 2021, update 10 March 2022)
note: How digital audience targeting works and its alternatives to third-party cookies: contextual targeting, first-party/identity solutions, data clean rooms, telco data, Google Topics; effects on measurement and verification. Note: Google kept third-party cookies in Chrome (April 2025) and retired Privacy Sandbox (Oct 2025) - discuss what remains relevant (consent, first-party data, contextual).
course_use: Background reading for the digital targeting session; free PDF (2.35 MB).

title: Update on Plans for Privacy Sandbox Technologies
author_source: Anthony Chavez (Google, VP Privacy Sandbox); official Google blog post, 17 Oct 2025
note: Primary source on the end of Google's cookie-deprecation path: after keeping third-party cookie choice in Chrome (April 2025), Google retires Privacy Sandbox targeting/measurement APIs (incl. Topics, Protected Audience, Attribution Reporting) due to low adoption, keeping CHIPS, FedCM and Private State Tokens. Needed to update textbook claims about a 'cookieless future'.
course_use: Short case on technology and regulation as drivers of targeting practice; free.

title: IAB Austria Umfrage: Digitalwirtschaft in der Post-Cookie-Ära (2025)
author_source: IAB Austria, AG Programmatic Advertising / Sub-AG Post-Third-Party-Cookie-Ära; member survey, May 2025 (second wave after 2023), reported by Leadersnet
note: Austrian market view: 60% of companies feel very well prepared for a cookieless future (2023: 47%); 53% see reducing third-party cookies as the right step; most action taken in targeting (73.7%) and measurement/analytics (68.4%). Local data point on Austrian targeting practice.
course_use: Austrian context slide; free; IAB Austria (iab.at) also a source of guest speakers.

title: Ipsos Global Trends
author_source: Ipsos; global values and attitudes study (recurring; latest edition c. 2025, 50+ markets, incl. values-based global segments)
note: Large-scale attitudinal survey with macro trends and global values-based consumer segments; an example of cross-country psychographic segmentation and input for positioning against cultural trends.
course_use: Use selected charts in the psychographic segmentation discussion; free report download (registration).

title: 15.810 Marketing Management (Fall 2010): Lecture notes incl. 'Segmentation, targeting and positioning' and 'STP-based strategy'
author_source: Natalie Mizik, MIT OpenCourseWare, 2010, course website with PDF slides (20 sessions)
note: Session 6 (STP) and session 8 (STP-based strategy) are free PDF slide decks from an MBA core course; course framework places STP between situation analysis and the 4Ps, which mirrors a WU intro course structure. Session 4 (customer value, CLV) is a useful bridge to customer-value-based targeting.
course_use: Instructor prep and benchmarking of own slides; students can read lec06 as pre-reading. Free, CC BY-NC-SA.

title: Market Segmentation Analysis: companion site with R package MSA, datasets and step-by-step R demos
author_source: Sara Dolnicar, Bettina Grün, Friedrich Leisch, BOKU Vienna, companion website to the 2018 open-access Springer book
note: Download page for the MSA R package (v0.3-1) with R demo scripts for each of the book's 10 steps (steps 4-10 in code) plus the McDonald's fast-food case study; CSV datasets include Austrian winter vacation activities (1991/92, 1997/98), Australian travel motives, risk taking and fast-food perceptions. The Austrian tourism data and Vienna-based authors make it a strong local fit.
course_use: Lab session: replicate the fast-food case (k-means, segment profile plots, target selection) in R; homework on the Austrian winter-tourism data. Free (book CC BY 4.0).

title: scikit-learn User Guide 2.3: Clustering (incl. comparison of algorithms and evaluation metrics)
author_source: scikit-learn developers, scikit-learn.org, continuously updated documentation website
note: Overview table of 12 clustering methods (k-means, Ward/agglomerative, DBSCAN, Gaussian mixtures, etc.) with use cases and scalability, the well-known algorithm comparison figure, and a section on evaluation metrics (silhouette coefficient, adjusted Rand index, etc.) with copy-paste code. Good reference for why 'segments' depend on algorithm choice.
course_use: Reference for Python lab sessions on data-driven segmentation; show comparison figure in class to discuss algorithm choice. Free.

title: scikit-learn example: Selecting the number of clusters with silhouette analysis on KMeans clustering
author_source: scikit-learn developers, scikit-learn.org, documentation example (runnable code + plots)
note: Runnable script producing silhouette plots for k = 2 to 6 side by side with the cluster scatter; illustrates visually why a statistically 'best' k may still not be managerially meaningful.
course_use: Lab: students adapt the script to customer data and justify their chosen number of segments. Free.

title: Claritas MyBestSegments: PRIZM Premier ZIP Code Lookup and Segment Explorer
author_source: Claritas, claritas360.claritas.com, interactive geodemographic website
note: Free ZIP lookup returns the top 5 PRIZM Premier segments (68 segments in total) for any US ZIP code with lifestyle, media and purchase snapshots (e.g. 'Upper Crust'). Concrete demonstration of geodemographic segmentation and its limits (describes places, not individuals).
course_use: Warm-up: students look up famous US ZIP codes (e.g. 90210, 10001) and compare segments; discuss transferability to Austria. Free (some tabs subscriber-only).

title: VALS Survey (US framework): take the survey and read the eight VALS types
author_source: Strategic Business Insights (SBI), strategicbusinessinsights.com, interactive psychographic survey website
note: Students answer the short VALS questionnaire and receive a primary and secondary type from the eight-type framework (Innovators, Thinkers, Believers, Achievers, Strivers, Experiencers, Makers, Survivors) on resources x primary motivation axes. Classic self-test for psychographic segmentation; US-normed, so a good starting point for critique.
course_use: In-class or pre-class activity: take survey, compare types in groups, then critique validity vs. behavioural segmentation. Free; site was unreachable from our test environment, verify before class.

title: Sinus-Milieus: Zielgruppenmodell (Deutschland, Österreich, Schweiz, international Meta-Milieus)
author_source: SINUS-Institut (Heidelberg/Berlin), sinus-institut.de, website, German
note: Official description of the 10 German Sinus-Milieus (model updated end of 2021) on social status x basic values axes, plus links to country models and international Meta-Milieus (9 milieus each for established and emerging markets, 40+ countries). Free info brochure download and explainer video; the German-speaking standard for lifestyle segmentation.
course_use: Pre-reading before a session on psychographic segmentation; students position brands on the milieu map. Free (detailed Infopakete paid).

title: Sinus-Milieus in Österreich (INTEGRAL model, update October 2022)
author_source: SINUS-Institut / INTEGRAL Markt- und Meinungsforschung (Vienna), sinus-institut.de, website, German
note: Lists the 10 Austrian milieus with population shares, e.g. Adaptiv-Pragmatische Mitte 14%, Nostalgisch-Bürgerliche 12%, Hedonisten 11%, Postmaterielle 11%, Performer 9%, Kosmopolitische Individualisten 6%. Model used in Austria since 2001; links to the Austrian explainer video and Infopakete.
course_use: Exercise: which Austrian milieus would you target for a given Austrian brand (e.g. Manner, Red Bull, A1), and how would positioning differ? Free.

title: PerceptualMaps.com: free perceptual map templates and guides
author_source: Geoff Fripp, perceptualmaps.com, website with Excel templates and articles
note: Free Excel perceptual map maker (up to 50 brands), multi-map maker, MDS and overall-similarities gap map templates, brand-association map template; guides on choosing determinant attributes, competitive sets and reading positioning gaps. Paid MDS tool for a small fee.
course_use: Lab / group work: build a perceptual map of Austrian supermarkets or banks from a quick class survey. Free templates.

title: The Value Proposition Canvas (official tool page and free PDF)
author_source: Strategyzer (Osterwalder et al.), strategyzer.com, tool website
note: Free high-resolution canvas download; customer profile (jobs, pains, gains) vs. value map (pain relievers, gain creators). Useful for linking segment needs to a positioning/value proposition. Page also upsells a USD 299/year playbook subscription (not needed).
course_use: Workshop: after choosing a target segment, teams fill in the canvas to derive a positioning statement. Free PDF.

title: R for Marketing Research and Analytics: companion website (code, data, slides, exercises)
author_source: Chris Chapman & Elea McDonnell Feit, r-marketing.r-forge.r-project.org, book companion site (2nd ed. 2019)
note: Free .R code, data files, classroom slides and exercises for the book; the chapter 'Segmentation: Clustering and Classification' walks through a simulated consumer segment dataset with hierarchical clustering, k-means, mixture models and classification of new customers.
course_use: Lab material for an R-based segmentation session; slides can be reused with attribution. Free (site hosted on R-Forge; was not reachable in our test).

title: AMA Marketing Definitions: Segmentation and Targeting
author_source: American Marketing Association, ama.org, glossary web page
note: Authoritative short definitions of segmentation and targeting from the AMA dictionary; handy for aligning terminology at course start.
course_use: Glossary link in the course syllabus; quick quiz warm-up. Free.

title: Ehrenberg-Bass Institute for Marketing Science (news and insights)
author_source: Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, University of South Australia, marketingscience.info, institute website
note: Home of Byron Sharp's 'How Brands Grow' school: concepts of mental and physical availability, Category Entry Points and distinctive assets, plus a news-and-insights archive with articles critical of conventional segmentation. Provides the evidence-based counterpoint to textbook STP.
course_use: Source for a debate session (Kotler STP vs. Sharp 'sophisticated mass marketing'). Mostly free; some research reports for members only.

title: Mark Ritson: Marketing Week columnist archive
author_source: Mark Ritson, Marketing Week, columnist page (weekly columns since 2010)
note: Index of all Ritson columns, many on segmentation, targeting, positioning, differentiation vs. distinctiveness and the 'two-speed' targeting model; useful for picking current, provocative readings each semester.
course_use: Instructor resource to select weekly provocation readings. Many columns free; some require free registration or subscription.

title: Gründerplattform: Sinus-Milieus (Zielgruppen verstehen)
author_source: Gründerplattform (BMWK and KfW initiative), gruenderplattform.de, guide page, German
note: Plain-German explainer of the Sinus-Milieus aimed at founders, with how to use milieus for target-group definition; accessible for bachelor students before reading the official SINUS material.
course_use: Pre-reading in German for a flipped-classroom session. Free.

title: Kaggle dataset: Mall Customer Segmentation Data (Mall_Customers.csv)
author_source: vjchoudhary7, Kaggle, dataset page (200 customers: gender, age, annual income, spending score)
note: Tiny, clean dataset widely used in k-means tutorials; five income x spending-score clusters are visible by eye, so students can check algorithm output against intuition before moving to messier transaction data.
course_use: First hands-on clustering exercise (30 min) in Python/R/Excel. Free with Kaggle login for download.

title: Mark Ritson: Segmentation is not the prerequisite for success
author_source: Chris Sutcliffe reporting Mark Ritson's Festival of Marketing keynote, Marketing Week, 5 Oct 2023, news article
note: Ritson argues ~90% of segmentations are not fit for purpose because markets are more homogeneous than assumed; targeting has diminishing returns; proposes 'two speeds' (mass brand building + targeted activation). Examples: Ladder/Money Dashboard ad test (simplest ad won in all segments), Tesco Clubcard, KitKat 'Have a break'.
course_use: Provocation reading before the segmentation session; class debate 'Is segmentation pointless?'. Free (registration may be requested).

title: Mark Ritson: Only crap marketers mistake stereotypes for segments
author_source: Mark Ritson, Marketing Week, 26 Jul 2017, opinion column
note: Critique of 'millennials' as a segment, citing Schiere's study of ~15,000 millennials in 20+ countries spread across all attitudinal groups; Air France-KLM's millennial airline Joon as a failed segment-based launch; criteria that real segments must be empirically distinct.
course_use: Discussion of segmentation criteria (measurable, distinct, actionable); homework: critique a generational segmentation from Austrian media. Free/login.

title: Mark Ritson: Targeting or mass marketing? The answer is both
author_source: Mark Ritson, Marketing Week, 2 Aug 2018, opinion column
note: Reconciles Sharp's 'sophisticated mass marketing' with STP via Binet and Field's 60/40 split (long-term brand building to whole category, short-term activation to targets); recounts the 2017 Ritson vs. Sharp debate (59% vs. 27% audience vote); Apple ~87% of smartphone profits on ~18% of units as a targeting example.
course_use: Core reading for the targeting session; basis for a structured pro/contra debate. Free/login.

title: Mark Ritson: Ignore anyone who tells you to forget about targeting
author_source: Mark Ritson, Marketing Week, 19 Feb 2025, opinion column
note: Responds to platform/AI claims that targeting is obsolete: 'Targeting is the start of strategy'. Cites Braun & Schwartz on biased A/B tests in ad platforms and Better Briefs data (only a third of agencies leave a brief with a clear target). Example: Mini MBA deliberately excludes low-value audiences.
course_use: Current reading linking STP to AI-driven ad platforms (Advantage+, PMax); seminar discussion. Free/login.

title: Mark Ritson: Planning for marketing planning: 14 steps to an effective presentation
author_source: Mark Ritson, Marketing Week, 11 Feb 2021, opinion column
note: Very practical template: segmentation on one slide (segment size, value, share), targeting overlaid on it with 'two-speed' targets, and positioning as What / Versus / Is (2-3 associations) checked with a Three Cs test (customer, company, competitors).
course_use: Template for student group projects (STP section of a marketing plan). Free/login.

title: Mark Ritson: Differentiation is not about uniqueness
author_source: Mark Ritson, Marketing Week, opinion column
note: Argues for relative rather than unique differentiation: pick one positioning concept and put excess share of voice behind two or three attributes rather than 25; useful counter to USP-based textbook positioning.
course_use: Reading for the positioning session; exercise: reduce a brand's claims to 2-3 attributes. Free/login.

title: Mark Ritson: Three axioms and three questions that summarise all of brand strategy
author_source: Mark Ritson, Marketing Week, 2025, opinion column
note: Condenses brand strategy into 'Who are we targeting?', 'What is our positioning?' (two or three associations) and objectives; argues the short-term performance budget is best spent on specific target segments.
course_use: One-page summary reading for the STP wrap-up session. Free/login.

title: A quickstart guide to positioning
author_source: April Dunford, guest post in Lenny's Newsletter, 26 Jan 2021, blog post (~15 min read)
note: Dunford's five components in order: competitive alternatives, differentiated capabilities, value, target customer segment ('who cares a lot'), market category; rejects fill-in-the-blank positioning statements; traps such as phantom competitors and unnecessary new categories. B2B/tech oriented, contrasts nicely with Kotler/Ritson.
course_use: Flipped classroom: students apply the five steps to a WU-start-up or Austrian B2B firm. Free edition (no paywall).

title: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process (Lenny's Podcast)
author_source: Lenny Rachitsky with April Dunford, Lenny's Newsletter/Podcast, 9 Jun 2022, podcast episode with transcript
note: Covers how to tell if positioning is weak, the five-step process, and the difference between segmentation and personas, including the 'champion' persona in B2B buying.
course_use: Optional listening; useful to discuss segment vs. persona distinction. Free.

title: Positioning with April Dunford (newsletter)
author_source: April Dunford, Substack, ongoing newsletter
note: Regular posts and podcast episodes on positioning practice, best-fit customers vs. bad-fit customers, and sales narratives; practitioner perspective from 300+ technology companies.
course_use: Instructor resource for current positioning examples; optional student follow-up. Free (some posts paid).

title: How Superhuman Built an Engine to Find Product/Market Fit
author_source: Rahul Vohra, First Round Review, 13 Nov 2018, long-form article
note: Data-driven targeting in a start-up: Sean Ellis survey ('very disappointed' >= 40%), segmenting respondents to find the 'high-expectation customer' (HXC), and rebuilding the roadmap; score rose from 22% to 58%. Concrete, numeric example of choosing a target segment.
course_use: Case-style reading for targeting in start-ups; students design an Ellis survey for a campus app. Free.

title: Instead of segmentation, try inclusion: it will get you more sales
author_source: Campaign UK article republished by the Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, marketingscience.info, c. 2020, blog/news post
note: Ehrenberg-Bass position in brief: brand share bears little relationship to targeted segments, marketing is 'a size game', targeting should prioritise non-buyers; brands moving to broad targets such as 'anyone with a mouth'. No data shown, which itself is a teaching point.
course_use: Debate reading opposite Ritson columns; critical-thinking exercise on evidence quality. Free.

title: Data-driven customer segmentation (k-means, elbow, silhouette, marketing interpretation)
author_source: Towards Data Science, blog post (Python tutorial)
note: Walks through why segmentation matters, building k-means, selecting k via elbow and silhouette, and translating clusters into marketing personas; good bridge from code to managerial interpretation.
course_use: Pre-reading for a Python lab. Free (may hit Medium-style limits).

title: K-Means clustering with Mall Customer Segmentation Data: full detailed code and explanation
author_source: Analytics Vidhya, May 2021, blog tutorial (Python)
note: Step-by-step Python code on the Kaggle Mall Customers data (scaling, elbow method, 5-cluster solution, plots), suitable for students with little coding background.
course_use: Lab handout / homework code-along. Free.

title: Markenpositionierung: Strategien und Best Practices für den Wettbewerbsvorteil
author_source: Madlen Nicolay, OMR Reviews Contenthub, 8 Oct 2024, blog guide, German
note: German practitioner guide: types of positioning (functional, emotional, price, quality, innovation) with examples (Red Bull, IKEA, Dove, Patagonia, Netto, Bosch, Tesla), seven-step process and tools. Good for German-language vocabulary; less evidence-based than Ritson/Dunford.
course_use: Contrast reading: compare OMR's USP-centred view with Ritson's relative differentiation. Free.

title: Sinus-Milieus: So finden Sie die richtige Zielgruppe
author_source: HubSpot Blog Deutschland, blog post, German
note: Explains the 10 Sinus-Milieus and the 'Digitale Sinus-Milieus' for online campaigns, with practical steps to use milieus for target-group definition and content marketing.
course_use: German pre-reading for the lifestyle-segmentation session. Free.

title: Zielgruppen: Lebensstile, Marken, Werte. Zielmärkte lassen sich über verschiedene Ansätze bestimmen
author_source: Manuela Gemmrig, absatzwirtschaft (print archive), 2009, article, German
note: German overview of segmentation bases (geographic incl. micro-geography, socio-demographic, psychographic, behavioural) and why single socio-demographic variables explain little purchase behaviour; dated but solid conceptual summary.
course_use: Optional German reading on bases of segmentation. Free (archive).

title: Veränderte Gesellschaft: Neue Sinus-Milieus für Österreich
author_source: HORIZONT Österreich editorial team, horizont.at, 23 Nov 2022, news article, German
note: Reports INTEGRAL's 2022 update of the Austrian milieu model: polarisation between future- and past-oriented outlooks, driven less by age than by differing societal ideals; Austrian trade-press framing of the model.
course_use: Local context for the Sinus session; pair with the official Austria page. Partly paywalled.

title: Sinus-Milieus schaffen Werberelevanz in den Zielgruppen
author_source: HORIZONT (Germany), e-paper issue 02/2025, article, German
note: Trade-press piece on using Sinus-Milieus to differentiate broad target groups and on how milieus behave online, with agency practice (DDB Germany).
course_use: Optional current trade-press example. Paid / subscription.

title: StatQuest: K-means clustering
author_source: Josh Starmer, StatQuest with Josh Starmer, YouTube, 2018, video, 8:30 min
note: Visual explanation of the k-means algorithm, choosing k with an elbow plot, k-means vs. hierarchical clustering, 2-D data and heatmaps; R demo code on GitHub (StatQuest/k_means_clustering_demo).
course_use: Flipped classroom before the clustering lab. Free.

title: StatQuest: Hierarchical Clustering
author_source: Josh Starmer, StatQuest with Josh Starmer, YouTube, 2017, video, 11:19 min
note: Explains agglomerative clustering, distance and linkage choices, and dendrograms; the conceptual basis for Ward + k-means two-step segmentation common in marketing research.
course_use: Pre-watching before the MSA/R lab. Free.

title: StatQuest: Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Step-by-Step
author_source: Josh Starmer, StatQuest with Josh Starmer, YouTube, 2018, video, 21:57 min
note: Step-by-step PCA intuition (projection, eigenvectors, scree plot); needed to understand attribute-based perceptual maps and dimension reduction before clustering. Short 6-min 'main ideas' version also available (HMOI_lkzW08).
course_use: Pre-watching for the perceptual-mapping session. Free.

title: StatQuest: PCA in Python
author_source: Josh Starmer, StatQuest with Josh Starmer, YouTube, 2018, video, 11:37 min
note: Code-along: PCA with scikit-learn, scree plot and 2-D PCA plot; directly reusable to build a perceptual map from brand x attribute ratings.
course_use: Lab code-along; students then plot brands from a class survey. Free.

title: Drawing and Interpreting Heatmaps
author_source: Josh Starmer, StatQuest with Josh Starmer, YouTube, 2016, video, 16:48 min
note: Shows the arbitrary choices (scaling, clustering, colour) behind cluster heatmaps; useful when students profile segments with heatmaps of segment means.
course_use: Optional for the segment-profiling step. Free.

title: Positioning in Crowded Markets: How to Make Any Offering Obviously Awesome
author_source: April Dunford, Wynter Games talk, YouTube (Wynter), Dec 2020, video, 47:48 min
note: Full talk of Dunford's positioning method: market context makes value obvious, five components from competitive alternatives to market category, examples of products that turned around by changing context.
course_use: Flipped classroom for the positioning session; students take notes on the five components. Free.

title: How to Position Your Product (Positioning Jujitsu) by April Dunford at Lean Product Meetup
author_source: April Dunford, Lean Product Meetup (Dan Olsen), YouTube, Sep/Oct 2020, video, 40:30 min
note: Focuses on positioning against powerful competitors: picking the segment where you are best, reframing the category, and using competitive alternatives as the anchor.
course_use: Alternative/extra talk; good for start-up-oriented students. Free.

title: Positioning that clicks with April Dunford
author_source: April Dunford, Alberta Innovates (Alberta Innovation Network), YouTube, Dec 2020, video, 60:13 min
note: One-hour session with Q&A on the Obviously Awesome method; Q&A covers start-up segment choice and repositioning.
course_use: Optional extended version for interested students. Free.

title: Marketing Deconstructed: Cutting the Bullsh*t and Getting Back to the Essential Strategic Tools
author_source: Mark Ritson, AANA/MCN lecture, YouTube (Australian Association of National Advertisers), 2016, video, 69:03 min
note: Full Ritson lecture to 400+ practitioners on strategic fundamentals (diagnosis, segmentation, targeting, positioning) vs. tactics; his trademark style, strong for motivating why STP matters.
course_use: Watch selected 15-20 min before the STP block; discussion questions on strategy vs. tactics. Free.

title: Making a Marketer 2: Lessons from the World's Top Marketers
author_source: Marketing Festival (Brno), YouTube, Oct 2024, feature-length documentary, 86:00 min
note: Documentary with Byron Sharp, Mark Ritson, Tom Roach and others including a chapter on STP vs. Ehrenberg-Bass approaches, plus SME strategy and AI.
course_use: Screen the STP chapter in class to launch the Sharp vs. Ritson debate. Free.

title: The power of Apple's brand positioning
author_source: Mark Ritson, Marketing Week (Effie 50 years series), YouTube, 2019, video, 9:55 min
note: Ritson explains Apple's positioning around three tenets (simplicity, creativity, humanity) and how Chiat/Day executed it; concise worked example of 'two or three associations'.
course_use: In-class example for positioning; students derive a positioning for a rival brand in 3 words. Free.

title: The effectiveness of Gillette's marketing strategy
author_source: Mark Ritson, Marketing Week (Effie 50 years series), YouTube, 2019, video, 9:52 min
note: Case of combining mass marketing with targeted campaigns (two-speed targeting) to build Gillette; supports the 'targeting or mass? both' argument.
course_use: In-class case for the targeting session. Free.

title: Two-Thirds of American Marketers Would Fail a Basic Marketing Test (with Mark Ritson)
author_source: The Marketing Architects Podcast, YouTube, Jun 2026, video podcast, 39:35 min
note: Ritson presents Ipsos research: more than 40% of US marketers cannot define positioning while 84% rate themselves above average; formal training as the strongest predictor of competence.
course_use: Motivational opener for the positioning session (first 10 min). Free.

title: Top Brand Strategy Secrets from Mark Ritson
author_source: Brand Tuned Podcast, YouTube, May 2024, video podcast, 31:25 min
note: Chaptered interview: market research process (12:11), brand vs. marketing strategy (15:40), distinctiveness vs. differentiation (17:42); concise practitioner view on positioning.
course_use: Optional homework listening with timestamps. Free.

title: How Brands Grow With Marketing Science (Prof. Byron Sharp)
author_source: Byron Sharp, Brand Master Academy, YouTube, Apr 2024, video interview, 47:56 min
note: Sharp on mental and physical availability, reaching all category buyers and why heavy segmentation/targeting limits growth; timestamped chapters.
course_use: Pre-watching for the 'anti-targeting' side of the debate. Free.

title: SBP 215: What Marketers Still Get Wrong, with Prof. Byron Sharp
author_source: Sleeping Barber marketing podcast, YouTube, Jul 2026, video podcast, 26:00 min
note: Recorded at Cannes 2026 after Sharp's joint session with Ritson; covers the five fundamentals they agree on and where the industry still errs, a useful update showing convergence between the camps.
course_use: Recent follow-up for the debate; short enough for homework. Free.

title: The Long and Short of It: publication launch
author_source: Les Binet & Peter Field, Institute of Practitioners in Advertising (IPA), YouTube, Jun 2013, video, 104 min
note: Binet and Field present IPA Databank evidence on balancing long-term brand building (broad reach) and short-term activation (targeted); source of the 60/40 rule Ritson uses to reconcile targeting with mass marketing.
course_use: Instructor background; show 10-15 min excerpt on reach vs. targeting. Free.

title: Understanding the Job (milkshake example)
author_source: Clayton Christensen, University of Phoenix lecture series excerpt, YouTube, 2016 upload, video, 4:55 min
note: Christensen tells the milkshake story: segmenting by the job customers 'hire' a product for rather than by demographics; ideal 5-min hook for needs/benefit-based segmentation.
course_use: Warm-up at the start of the segmentation-bases session. Free.

title: Sinus-Milieus einfach erklärt (Erklärvideo / Explainer video)
author_source: SINUS-Institut, YouTube, Feb 2023, video, 3:55 min, German with English subtitles
note: Official explainer of the milieu model (social status x basic values), example milieus and marketing uses (personas, touchpoints).
course_use: Warm-up for the lifestyle segmentation session. Free.

title: Sinus-Milieus in Österreich einfach erklärt (Erklärvideo / Explainer video)
author_source: SINUS-Institut / INTEGRAL, YouTube, Dec 2023, video, 3:39 min, German
note: Austria-specific explainer of the 10 Austrian milieus from the 2022 INTEGRAL update; direct local relevance for WU students.
course_use: Show in class, then students locate themselves and Austrian brands on the map. Free.

title: How to Make a Perceptual Map (Positioning Map) in Excel
author_source: Teaching Junction, YouTube, Jan 2021, video, 16:14 min
note: Step-by-step building of a two-attribute positioning map as an Excel scatter chart with brand labels; low-tech entry point before PCA/MDS-based maps.
course_use: Lab / homework: build a positioning map for Austrian supermarkets or mobile operators. Free.

title: How to Use the MDS Perceptual Map Template
author_source: Marketing Study Guide (perceptualmaps.com), YouTube, 2014, video, 6:10 min
note: Shows how to create multidimensional (MDS-style) maps comparing several brands on several attributes with the free template; companion 'Top 12 tips for analyzing perceptual maps' video (f3jHx2I62eo, 17:35 min).
course_use: Lab with the perceptualmaps.com template. Free.

title: RFM Analysis Tutorial in Pandas: Simple Customer Segmentation Analysis
author_source: Jie Jenn, YouTube, Apr 2023, video, 17:18 min
note: Code-along computing recency, frequency and monetary scores in pandas and combining them into rule-based segments; dataset linked for follow-along.
course_use: Lab on behavioural segmentation with transaction data. Free.

title: Full Python Tutorial: Customer Lifetime Value & RFM Analysis using Machine Learning
author_source: Matt Dancho, Business Science, YouTube, Jul 2021, video, 1:43:52 h
note: Extended code-along from RFM features to predicting 90-day purchase probability and spend; links segmentation to customer-value-based targeting.
course_use: Advanced/optional lab for analytics-track students. Free.

title: Customer Segmentation in Python
author_source: Karolis Urbonas, DataCamp, online course, ~4 h (17 videos, 55 exercises)
note: Uses real online-retailer transaction data: cohort analysis, RFM segments, data preparation for clustering, k-means and segment profiling; interactive browser exercises.
course_use: Homework track for analytics students. First chapter free; full course paid (DataCamp Premium approx. USD 25-40/month; free DataCamp Classrooms for instructors).

title: Machine Learning for Marketing in Python
author_source: DataCamp, online course, ~4 h (16 videos, 53 exercises)
note: Four chapters: ML basics, churn prediction, CLV prediction, customer segmentation based on product purchase patterns; shows how segmentation feeds into targeting models.
course_use: Optional follow-up to the clustering lab. First chapter free; rest paid (DataCamp subscription or DataCamp Classrooms).

title: Foundations of Marketing Analytics
author_source: Arnaud De Bruyn, ESSEC Business School, Coursera, MOOC, ~5 h (5 modules)
note: Module 1 statistical segmentation (hierarchical clustering, choosing number of segments, RFM), Module 2 managerial segmentation, Module 3 targeting and scoring models, Module 4 CLV; R/RStudio recitals.
course_use: Self-study complement for an R-based segmentation lab. Free to enrol (limited access); certificate via Coursera Plus (approx. EUR 50/month).

title: Introduction to Marketing (Wharton): Branding module 'Marketing Strategy and Brand Positioning'
author_source: Barbara Kahn, Peter Fader et al., University of Pennsylvania (Wharton), Coursera, MOOC, ~10 h
note: Kahn's module on marketing strategy and brand positioning (positioning statements, perceptual maps, repositioning) and Fader's customer-centricity module (heterogeneity of customer value as a basis for targeting).

title: Customer Analytics (Wharton)
author_source: Eric Bradlow, Peter Fader, Raghu Iyengar, University of Pennsylvania, Coursera, MOOC, ~10 h
note: Covers descriptive, predictive and prescriptive customer analytics; connects segmentation and targeting with data on customer behaviour; very widely used (300k+ learners).
course_use: Optional MOOC for analytics-interested students. Free audit with login; certificate paid.

title: Positioning: What you need for a successful Marketing Strategy (Marketing Strategy Specialization, course 2)
author_source: IE Business School, Coursera, MOOC, ~11 h
note: Course on analysing customer segments to identify target markets, developing differentiation and value propositions, and applying positioning frameworks/tools to define and evaluate a brand position; part of a 5-course specialization with capstone.

title: Developing a Winning Marketing Strategy
author_source: Hayden Noel, Maria Rodas, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Coursera, MOOC, ~20 h (4 modules)
note: Includes a module on segmentation, targeting and positioning in the value-creation stage of marketing strategy; academic-style explanation suitable for bachelor level.

title: Kaggle notebook: Customer Segmentation with RFM (KMeans and Hierarchical)
author_source: Yasemin Turker, Kaggle, Python notebook (Online Retail II data)
note: Complete RFM pipeline with k-means and agglomerative clustering, evaluated with silhouette and Davies-Bouldin; students can fork and run in the browser without installation.

author_source: gdeagle19, Kaggle, Python notebook (Online Retail II data)

course_use: Lab extension on making clusters actionable/interpretable. Free with Kaggle login.

title: Mini MBA in Marketing
author_source: Mark Ritson, Marketing Week Mini MBA, online course (~12 weeks, modules on research, segmentation, targeting, positioning, objectives, 4Ps)

title: Market Segmentation, Target Market Selection, and Positioning (Background Note 506-019)
author_source: Miklos Sarvary, Anita Elberse; Harvard Business School, 2005 (rev. 2006); background note, 5 pages; approx. USD 5-12 (also sold via Ivey at approx. USD 11.64)
