course_use: Pre-reading for session 1 of the STP block; pair with Fashion Channel or Chase Sapphire. Paid (approx. USD 5-12 per student); WU-Lizenz prüfen (HBP coursepack).

title: The Fashion Channel: Market Segmentation (Brief Case 2075)
author_source: Wendy Stahl; Harvard Business Publishing Brief Case, 2007; 12 pages; case preview, updated teaching note (incl. undergraduate section) and audio version; approx. USD 5-9
note: New marketing VP of a cable fashion network must choose among three segmentation scenarios (e.g. broad vs. focused audience segments) with consumer research and advertiser economics in exhibits; no single dominant answer. Teaches segment attractiveness, segment profitability arithmetic and the link to positioning for viewers and advertisers.
course_use: Classic first STP case for undergraduates; group work computing segment value, then plenary vote. Paid (approx. USD 5-9); WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Chase Sapphire: Creating a Millennial Cult Brand (Case 518-024)
author_source: Shelle Santana, Jill Avery, Christine Snively; Harvard Business School, 2017 (rev. 2023); case with teaching note; approx. USD 5-12
note: JPMorgan Chase designed the Sapphire Reserve card for affluent millennials; after hitting its 12-month target in two weeks, managers must retain bonus-driven customers and find positioning gaps among Sapphire products. Teaches targeting a generational segment, product-line positioning and the risks of acquisition incentives.
course_use: Targeting/positioning session; perceptual map exercise of Sapphire vs. Amex/Citi. Listed in HBP Course Explorer STP module. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Metabical: Positioning and Communications Strategy for a New Weight Loss Drug (Brief Case 4240)
author_source: John A. Quelch, Heather Beckham; Harvard Business Publishing Brief Case, 2010; 12 pages; case preview, updated teaching note with undergraduate section, audio; approx. USD 5-9
note: Pre-launch: marketing director must pick the target (moderately overweight adults, BMI 25-30) and write a positioning statement and push/pull communication plan for physicians and consumers. Classic for writing a positioning statement and choosing among segments defined by need and decision-making unit; companion case 4183 covers pricing.
course_use: Students write a positioning statement in groups and compare; works as exam case. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: HubSpot: Inbound Marketing and Web 2.0 (Case 509-049)
author_source: Thomas Steenburgh, Jill Avery, Naseem Dahod; Harvard Business School, 2009 (rev. 2011); 21 pages; teaching note 510-043; approx. USD 5.10 per student (HBP educator price)
note: B2B SaaS start-up must decide which persona to serve: 'Owner Ollie' (small business owner) vs. 'Marketer Mary' (marketer in mid-size firm). Exhibits allow customer lifetime value per segment, so students see targeting as an economic choice; also pricing and channel implications. Case Centre award 2014, Classic Case Collection.
course_use: Strong B2B targeting case; group work computing CLV by persona, debate which segment to drop. Paid (approx. USD 5); WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Aqualisa Quartz: Simply a Better Shower (Case 502-030)
author_source: Youngme Moon, Kerry Herman; Harvard Business School, 2002 (rev. 2022); 19 pages; teaching note 503-058; video supplement 506-706; approx. USD 5-12
note: UK shower maker launches a superior product that does not sell. Decision: which segment to target first (plumbers, DIY, developers, premium consumers) given channel influence of plumbers. Shows that targeting must include intermediaries and that positioning must be built around the gatekeeper's benefits (installation time, profitability).
course_use: Best-seller; whole-session case discussion on choosing a beachhead segment; video supplement for wrap-up. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Mountain Man Brewing Co.: Bringing the Brand to Light (Brief Case 2069)
author_source: Harvard Business Publishing Brief Case; approx. 10 pages; teaching note available; approx. USD 5-9
note: Regional lager brand with an older blue-collar core must decide whether to launch a light beer to reach younger drinkers. Teaches targeting a new segment vs. protecting the core, cannibalisation and brand-positioning stretch; includes market data for break-even calculations.
course_use: Undergraduate case for targeting vs. brand dilution; quick break-even group work. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen. Link is a catalogue listing; buy via HBP.

title: Harrah's Entertainment, Inc. (Case 502-011)
author_source: Rajiv Lal (with Patricia Martone Carrolo); Harvard Business School, 2001/2002 (rev. 2004); approx. 20 pages; teaching note available; approx. USD 5-12
note: Casino operator uses Total Rewards database and predicted customer worth (not observed play) to segment and tier customers (Gold/Platinum/Diamond). Teaches behavioural/value-based segmentation, CRM targeting and whether data-driven segmentation is a replicable advantage. Pair with Loveman's HBR article 'Diamonds in the Data Mine' (2003).
course_use: Data-driven segmentation session; discuss 'customer worth' vs. demographics. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Dove: Evolution of a Brand (Case 508-047)
author_source: John A. Deighton; Harvard Business School, 2007 (rev. 2008); 13 pages; teaching note 508-109; video advertising supplement 508-704; ECCH award 2012; approx. USD 5-12
note: Dove moves from a functional soap (one-quarter moisturising cream) to a masterbrand with a point of view (Real Beauty). Teaches repositioning from functional to emotional/social benefits, brand extension under one positioning, and loss of control over meaning in social media.
course_use: Positioning/repositioning session with video supplement; debate on 'purpose' positioning. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Progressive Corp. (Case 797-109)
author_source: Michael E. Porter, Nicolaj Siggelkow; Harvard Business School, 1997; approx. 25 pages; approx. USD 5-12
note: Insurer profitably targets the non-standard (high-risk) auto segment through superior risk segmentation and pricing; must respond when leader Allstate enters its segment. Shows segmentation as a source of competitive advantage (finer risk cells) and the defensibility of a niche target.
course_use: Advanced/strategy-oriented targeting case; good for linking STP to competitive strategy. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Understanding Customer Profitability at Charles Schwab (Case 106-002)
author_source: F. Asis Martinez-Jerez; Harvard Business School, 2005 (rev. 2011); approx. 15 pages; approx. USD 5-12
note: Activity-based costing reveals profitability by customer segment and individual, informing segment-specific pricing and service decisions. Useful to show that segments must be evaluated on profitability, not only size.
course_use: Segment-evaluation session; cross-listed with management accounting. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Charles Schwab & Co., Inc.: The 'Talk to Chuck' Advertising Campaign (Case 507-005)
author_source: John A. Quelch, Laura Winig; Harvard Business School, 2007 (rev. 2008); approx. 20 pages; approx. USD 5-12
note: How Schwab differentiates itself in cluttered financial services: advertising objectives, message strategy (positioning against commission-driven brokers), media selection, metrics. Good bridge from positioning to communication; financial-services analogue for Erste Bank/Raiffeisen discussions.
course_use: Positioning-to-communication session; compare with Austrian banks' positioning. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Red Bull: The Anti-Brand Brand (CS-04-006)
author_source: Nader Tavassoli, Nirmalya Kumar, Sophie Linguri; London Business School, 2005; 11 pages; ECCH Marketing and Overall award, Classic Case Collection; price on login (approx. GBP 8-12)
note: In 2004 Red Bull held about 70% of global energy drinks, built among 18-35-year-olds via buzz, sponsorship and extreme sports. Decision: chase mainstream customers as Coca-Cola, Pepsi and private labels enter, without destroying the anti-brand mystique. Austrian brand; teaches niche-to-mass targeting dilemma and positioning consistency.
course_use: Austrian anchor case for whole session; follow up with 'Red Bull Spreads Its Wiiings'. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen (Case Centre).

title: Red Bull Spreads Its Wiiings (CS-22-016)
author_source: Nader Tavassoli; London Business School, 2022/2023; Case Centre Marketing award 2025; teaching slides with videos from cases@london.edu; price via Case Centre/HBP
note: Examines fit between the Red Bull core brand and extensions (The Organics by Red Bull, AlphaTauri fashion, F1 team). Teaches whether positioning can stretch to new segments and categories and brand-extension (dis)synergies.
course_use: Follow-up to Anti-Brand Brand; group work rating extension fit. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Dollar Shave Club: Disrupting the Shaving Industry (CS-18-017 / LBS150)
author_source: Nader Tavassoli, Karin Kollenz-Quetard, Jamie Anderson; London Business School, 2018; Case Centre Overall Winner 2021; teaching note with online-delivery tips; USD 11.95 at HBR Store
note: Challenger without patents targets men annoyed by overpriced, locked-up razors with a DTC subscription and humorous positioning against Gillette; ends with P&G/Gillette weighing a response to Unilever's acquisition interest. Teaches challenger positioning, targeting an underserved segment, and incumbent response.
course_use: Works in 45 min or longer; ideal for positioning against the leader. Paid (USD 11.95); WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Skoda Auto (A): Rebuilding the Brand / (B): Brand Turnaround Post-script
author_source: INSEAD case (ref. 5161), early 2000s; (B) 13 pages; via INSEAD Publishing and The Case Centre; approx. EUR 10-15
note: Skoda UK must launch the Fabia while 60-70% of car buyers reject the brand. Decision on target group, positioning and marketing mix to raise consideration; (B) reports the 'It's a Skoda. Honest' outcome. Excellent European repositioning case (VW group, CEE brand), aimed at introductory marketing.
course_use: Repositioning case discussion; pair with IPA/WARC Skoda paper as outcome evidence. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Michel et Augustin 2: Savour the Difference - Evaluating Brand Targeting and Positioning
author_source: F. Oble; ESSEC Business School, 2016; part 2 of a 4-case series with survey data and founder videos; via The Case Centre; approx. EUR 10-15
note: French challenger food brand; students diagnose its position in the yoghurt-drinks market using qualitative and quantitative survey data, then derive targeting and positioning. European FMCG context, introductory level, includes consumer data.
course_use: Group work with survey data; exam-case candidate. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Emerge Magazine: The Business of Ethnic Publishing (M-0682)
author_source: Geraldine Henderson, Cheri D. Cannon; Darden School of Business, 2003; 18 pages; price on Darden store (approx. USD 5-10)
note: Ethnic-focused magazine; the case is explicitly designed to show the importance of market definition, segmentation, targeting and positioning, and to discuss marketplace diversity. Good for discussing ethnicity as a segmentation base and its ethics.
course_use: Case discussion on market definition and segment choice. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: A Note on Market Definition, Segmentation, and Targeting (UV7286) and Brand Positioning Statements (UV5792)
author_source: Darden School of Business technical notes; sold via HBP; approx. USD 5-9 each
note: Two compact Darden notes: one walks through market definition, segmentation and targeting as 'three of four steps' of marketing strategy; the companion (UV5792) shows how to write and test a brand positioning statement. Useful scaffolding for any case.
course_use: Pre-reading/toolkit; give positioning-statement template before Metabical or Chase Sapphire. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Red Bull and Energy Drinks 2010 (M-0826 / UV5791)
author_source: Paul W. Farris; Darden School of Business, 2011; 3 pages; approx. USD 5-9
note: Very short case: Red Bull spends roughly 40% of sales on marketing, largely extreme-sports events; frames evaluation of its positioning in a crowded energy-drink market. Quick in-class read.
course_use: In-class warm-up or short exam case (read in 10 minutes). Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: TiVo Segmentation Analytics (Kellogg 5-414-753, KEL932)
author_source: Moran Cerf; Kellogg School of Management, 2016; case with dataset; also in SAGE Business Cases (2017); approx. USD 5-9 via Kellogg/HBP
note: Students act as consultants segmenting the market for TiVo's DVR from realistic survey data (cluster analysis), then profile and choose segments for marketing strategy. One of few cases with hands-on data for the segmentation step.
course_use: Lab/group exercise with clustering in Excel, R or Python; good for graded assignment. Paid; SAGE edition possibly WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Auranis DermLab Serum (A): Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning with AI
author_source: Mohanbir Sawhney; Kellogg School of Management, 2026; case (A); price and teaching materials not shown on page
note: Brand-new case explicitly about running STP with AI tools for a skincare serum. Likely useful for discussing generative-AI-assisted segmentation and synthetic personas; content details not yet public, so review before adopting.
course_use: Candidate for an 'STP with AI' session; check availability via Kellogg Case Publishing/HBP. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Conglomerate Inc.'s New PDA (2001) - Marketing Engineering for Excel Case 1
author_source: Gary L. Lilien, Katrin Starke; DecisionPro / Marketing Engineering for Excel (ME-XL) v2; case plus dataset 'ConneCtor PDA 2001 Data (Segmentation).xls'; licence for ME-XL software required
note: Wireless carrier launches a PDA/smartphone hybrid ('ConneCtor'); students run needs-based cluster analysis and discriminant analysis on survey data, name and profile segments, and select targets (common answer: field-based segments such as 'Hard Hats', 'Service Pros'). Classic quantitative segmentation exercise paired with Lilien/Rangaswamy/De Bruyn textbook.
course_use: Computer-lab session on cluster-based segmentation; data can be re-run in R/Python. Paid software licence; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Ontela PicDeck (B): Customer Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning
author_source: SAGE Business Cases; tech start-up case (B part); length per SAGE listing; via institutional subscription
note: Start-up with a mobile imaging service (PicDeck) for wireless subscribers must choose segments, target and positioning. One of the few cases whose title covers the full STP sequence; good for new-tech/B2B2C targeting via carriers.
course_use: Group work on start-up STP. Access via SAGE Business Cases subscription; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Segmenting the Market for Wavin Plastics
author_source: Ross Brennan, Louise Canning, Raymond McDowell; SAGE Business Cases, 2014; with teaching notes
note: B2B segmentation of the UK market for plastic pipe systems (UK subsidiary of a European manufacturer). Teaches nested/B2B segmentation bases (industry, application, buying centre) as counterpart to consumer cases.
course_use: B2B segmentation session; pair with Brennan et al. B2B textbook chapter. Access via SAGE; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Mayora: Launching Coffee Joy
author_source: Emerald Emerging Markets Case Studies (EEMCS-10-2023-0412), 2024; case with teaching note for educators; approx. GBP 15-25 or via subscription
note: Indonesian biscuit launch: director must choose between a regional geographic target and urban, aspirational young consumers. Written explicitly for the STP module of postgraduate marketing courses; emerging-market context.
course_use: Case discussion or exam case on target selection. Paid or via EEMCS subscription; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Wise Minds: Risk Taking through Data Analytics
author_source: Emerald Emerging Markets Case Studies (EEMCS-07-2024-0298), 2024/2025; MBA case with dataset (11,882 apartments); teaching note for educators
note: Dubai real-estate brokerage must pick the most profitable customer segment using a large listings dataset. Combines segmentation analytics with targeting decision; good for data-driven STP.
course_use: Data lab / group assignment. Via EEMCS subscription; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Swarovski: How to Shine Through Stormy Weather?
author_source: Niccolo Pisani, Stephane Girod; IMD, 2023; via IMD and The Case Centre; approx. CHF/USD 10-15
note: Austrian crystal brand under its first external CEO (Alexis Nasard, 2022) seeks to restore performance and brand image; underlying move is repositioning to 'pop luxury' with tiered price/style segments (LUXignite). Austrian company; links repositioning, segment tiers and brand image.
course_use: Austrian repositioning case; pair with free IMD interview with Nasard. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Marketing Reading: Framework for Marketing Strategy Formation (Peloton launch) (8153)
author_source: Harvard Business Publishing Core Curriculum in Marketing, revised edition; reading with interactive illustrations; approx. USD 8-10
note: Uses Peloton's launch as running example for the 5Cs, segmentation, targeting, positioning and 4Ps. Good integrated reading that shows STP inside a full strategy framework with a familiar brand.
course_use: Core reading for the STP block; quiz on Peloton's target and positioning. Paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Classroom datasets: Customer Personality Analysis and Mall Customer Segmentation (Kaggle)
author_source: Kaggle community datasets (imakash3011; vjchoudhary7 et al.); free; CPA approx. 2,240 customers x 29 variables (demographics, spend by category, channel, campaign response); Mall approx. 200 customers x 5 variables
note: Free data for a do-it-yourself segmentation exercise: k-means or hierarchical clustering, segment profiling and naming, then target selection and positioning statement. The Mall dataset is a 30-minute toy example; CPA allows behavioural segmentation linked to campaign response (targeting).
course_use: Lab session or graded group assignment (Excel/R/Python); many public notebooks exist, so require own interpretation. Free (Kaggle login for download).

title: Online Retail II (UCI Machine Learning Repository) - RFM segmentation exercise
author_source: Daqing Chen; UCI Machine Learning Repository, donated 2019; 1,067,371 transactions of a UK online gift retailer 2009-2011; CC BY 4.0
note: Real transaction data for RFM (recency, frequency, monetary) and CLV-based behavioural segmentation of customers, including many wholesale buyers. Shows students how behavioural segments differ from demographic ones and how to target retention vs. acquisition.
course_use: Lab exercise or term project; free and openly licensed.

title: Avis 'We Try Harder' (1962) - positioning as No. 2
author_source: Doyle Dane Bernbach for Avis, 1962; summarised in Wikipedia entry on William Bernbach and trade histories; free
note: Avis turned its weaker market position versus Hertz into a positioning claim (No. 2, therefore we try harder). Reported results: from losses to profit within a year; tagline used for 50 years. Classic Ries/Trout example of relative positioning against the leader.
course_use: Warm-up for the positioning session; ask students for a 'No. 2' claim for an Austrian challenger brand. Free.

title: 7Up 'The Uncola' (1968) - positioning against a category
author_source: Claire Payton, Duke University Rubenstein Library (Hartman Center) blog, 2017; J. Walter Thompson archive material; free
note: 7Up was seen as a mixer/stomach remedy; JWT positioned it as the anti-establishment alternative to Coke and Pepsi rather than claiming similarity. Archive images of ads and billboards; also covers decline (lost share to Sprite, slogan dropped 1998), useful for discussing positioning wear-out.
course_use: Warm-up on positioning by contrast; show archive ads. Free.

title: Lucozade: A Case History (IPA Effectiveness Awards)
author_source: Ogilvy for SmithKline Beecham; IPA Effectiveness Awards case study (WARC); digital paper GBP 50 non-members / GBP 25 members
note: Repositioning from a convalescence drink to a fitness/energy drink for teenagers and young adults with Daley Thompson. First campaign failed in tracking; revised salience-led campaign delivered about 40% volume increase at equal weight, confirmed econometrically. Shows repositioning plus target shift with evidence.
course_use: Repositioning example with real effectiveness data; good for discussion of evidence. Paid (or WARC via WU-Lizenz prüfen).

title: Marlboro repositioning (1954) - from women's filter cigarette to the Marlboro Man
author_source: Leo Burnett for Philip Morris; Wikipedia 'Marlboro Man' and brand histories; free
note: Marlboro was a 'Mild as May' women's cigarette with under 1% share; Burnett re-targeted it to men with rugged archetypes, flip-top box and later 'Marlboro Country'. Dramatic case of changing target and positioning with the same product, and an ethics prompt (health-anxious smokers targeted).
course_use: Repositioning + ethics discussion. Free.

title: Old Spice 'The Man Your Man Could Smell Like' (2010) - targeting the buyer, not the user
author_source: Wieden+Kennedy for P&G; Grand Effie 2011, Cannes Film Grand Prix 2010; WARC news report; free news, full Effie case via WARC
note: Insight that women make roughly half or more of body-wash purchases led to targeting women as purchasers while repositioning an aging brand to younger men. Teaches distinguishing user, buyer and influencer in targeting, plus repositioning of a 'dad' brand.
course_use: Warm-up video plus discussion of decision-making unit. Free summary; full case WARC (WU-Lizenz prüfen).

title: Skoda 'It's a Skoda. Honest' - IPA effectiveness paper
author_source: Fallon London for Skoda UK; IPA Effectiveness Awards paper on WARC, early 2000s; paid
note: Documented outcome of the Skoda UK repositioning: confronting brand prejudice head-on with self-deprecating humour for the Fabia launch; improved consideration and reduced rejection. Complements the INSEAD Skoda case.
course_use: Use as 'what happened' reveal after the INSEAD case. WARC access: WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Dacia UK repositioning ('unconventional' value brand) - agency case
author_source: Vivaldi (brand consultancy), agency case study; free web page
note: Dacia was seen as 'cheap and cheerful' in the UK; brief was to emphasise smart value while building awareness and conversion. Illustrates positioning a low-price brand without stigma, relevant to Dacia's strong position in Austria and CEE.
course_use: Short example for value positioning; compare with Skoda. Free (agency self-report, treat critically).

title: Liquid Death - positioning water as a lifestyle/anti-brand
author_source: Beloved Brands (Graham Robertson), case analysis blog; free
note: Canned water positioned with heavy-metal imagery ('murder your thirst') and sustainability (aluminium) to target Gen Z/millennials and straight-edge music fans; deliberately breaks category codes. Good for discussing differentiation in commodity categories and risks of copycats/slowing growth.
course_use: Warm-up: map Liquid Death vs. Vöslauer/Römerquelle on a perceptual map. Free.

title: Oatly rebrand (2012 onwards) - from functional health product to lifestyle brand
author_source: Monocle, 'Against the grain' (Oatly CEO Toni Petersson profile); free web article
note: Under CEO Toni Petersson and creative director John Schoolcraft, Oatly abandoned generic health-food packaging for an irreverent anti-dairy voice and targeted early adopters (vegans, baristas) before going mainstream. Example of challenger positioning and beachhead targeting; includes dairy-industry lawsuit.
course_use: Short example in positioning session; compare Oatly vs. NÖM/Alpro. Free.

title: Dove 'Campaign for Real Beauty' - Quelch and Jocz analysis (free HBS PDF)
author_source: John A. Quelch, Katherine E. Jocz; HBS-hosted PDF chapter, 2008; free
note: Free analysis of Dove's mission to broaden the narrow definition of beauty and the 'Evolution' film's viral effect. Usable without buying the Deighton case to discuss purpose-based positioning and its credibility risks.
course_use: Free reading for the Dove positioning discussion. Free.

title: Swarovski as 'pop luxury' - IMD interview with CEO Alexis Nasard
author_source: I by IMD, interview article, 2023/2024; free
note: CEO explains repositioning the Austrian brand as 'pop luxury' with tiered product categories, price/style segmentation and cultural presence (flagships, collaborations) instead of raising prices across the board. Austrian real-world repositioning example.
course_use: Austrian example; pair with IMD Swarovski case or use alone for 15-min discussion. Free.

title: Almdudler 'Einkehrschwung' - relaunching an Austrian cult brand across target groups
author_source: House of Communication (agency) case page; free
note: After a long TV break, Almdudler revived the claim 'Wenn die kan Almdudler ham, geh i wieder ham' to regain top-of-mind and relevance among all Austrians while positioning the brand positively in many different target groups. Shows the mass-reach vs. targeting tension for a national brand.
course_use: Austrian warm-up: is broad reach the right choice? Free (agency self-report).

title: Manner - balancing Viennese tradition and younger target groups (WU Praxisdialog talk)
author_source: Handelszeitung, 9 April 2018, report on talk by Manner board member Alfred Schrott at the 50th WU 'Praxisdialog' (Prof. Peter Schnedlitz); free PDF on wu.ac.at
note: Manner keeps Vienna/Stephansdom tradition as core of the brand while adjusting communication (e.g. new voice-over) to appeal to younger consumers. WU-linked Austrian example of repositioning toward a new segment without losing the core.
course_use: Austrian example; possible guest-speaker lead. Free (German).

title: Hofer HoT launch - Effie Gold for a discounter's mobile private label
author_source: ESM Magazine report, 2016; agencies mediastrategen and Buero von List; free news
note: Hofer (Aldi Sued) launched HoT (Hofer Telekom) and won two Gold Effies in Austria. Useful to discuss how a discounter's price positioning transfers to a new category (telecom) and which segment it targets vs. A1, Magenta, Drei.
course_use: Austrian example for positioning transfer; students build a perceptual map of Austrian mobile brands. Free.

title: Sinus-Milieus Austria (INTEGRAL/SINUS) - lifestyle segmentation used by media and companies
author_source: pressetext, 'Praesentation der neuen Sinus-Milieus in einem veraenderten Oesterreich' (INTEGRAL), 2022; free
note: 2022 update of the Austrian Sinus-Milieus (survey of 1,000 Austrians aged 16-75) by INTEGRAL with SINUS; milieus plotted on social position x value orientation ('Kartoffelgrafik'), available down to census-district level. Prime example of psychographic segmentation that Austrian media sellers and brands use for targeting.
course_use: Lecture example; students place brands (e.g. Hofer, Manner, Tesla) into milieus. Free press info; detailed data paid.

title: Netflix micro-genres - 'How Netflix Reverse Engineered Hollywood'
author_source: Alexis C. Madrigal, The Atlantic, 2 January 2014; free article
note: Madrigal scraped 76,897 Netflix micro-genres and decoded their grammar; content is tagged by paid viewers on many scalar attributes. Shows product-side segmentation (content tagging) that enables fine-grained matching of offers to taste segments.
course_use: Warm-up: students generate micro-genres for their own viewing. Free.

title: Netflix taste clusters instead of demographics ('garbage heap')
author_source: Fortune, 27 March 2016 (based on Wired feature on Netflix's global algorithm); free article
note: Netflix groups viewers by shared taste, not age, gender or geography (Todd Yellin: demographics into the 'garbage heap'); e.g. 90% of anime viewing comes from outside Japan. Strong prompt to debate demographic vs. behavioural segmentation bases.
course_use: Discussion starter on segmentation bases. Free.

title: Tesco Clubcard and dunnhumby - Clubcard at 30
author_source: Computer Weekly feature 'Clubcard at 30: the evolution of retail loyalty', 2025; free
note: History of the loyalty card launched 1995: basket data combined with geodemographics (Acorn), then behavioural 'Lifestyles' segments (e.g. price-sensitive, convenience, finer foods) used for personalised coupons and ranging. Canonical example of behavioural segmentation at scale; compare with jö Bonus Club.
course_use: Lecture example; Austria comparison with jö and Hofer (no loyalty card). Free.

title: Amazon.com Recommendations: Item-to-Item Collaborative Filtering
author_source: Greg Linden, Brent Smith, Jeremy York; IEEE Internet Computing 7(1), 2003, pp. 76-80; industry report; free PDF copy at UMD
note: Primary source on how Amazon personalises its store for each customer ('segment of one'), and why item-to-item filtering scales better than cluster-based segmentation models. Lets students contrast classic segment-level targeting with individual-level personalisation.
course_use: Short reading for the 'end of segmentation?' debate. Free PDF copy (cs.umd.edu) / IEEE via WU-Lizenz.

title: P&G (Marc Pritchard, 2016): 'We targeted too much and went too narrow'
author_source: Fortune, 9 August 2016 (reporting WSJ interview); free news
note: P&G's CMO said hyper-targeted Facebook ads had become too narrow and the company shifted toward broader reach; he later clarified P&G was not cutting Facebook spend. Central real-world anchor for the precision-vs-reach debate (Ehrenberg-Bass vs. micro-targeting).
course_use: Debate prompt: assign teams 'narrow targeting' vs. 'mass reach'. Free.

title: Uncles et al. (2012): User profiles for directly competing brands seldom differ
author_source: Mark Uncles, Rachel Kennedy, Magda Nenycz-Thiel, Jaywant Singh, Simon Kwok; Journal of Advertising Research 52(2), 252-261; Ehrenberg-Bass; open repository copy at Kingston
note: Evidence across 25 years and 50 categories that buyers of competing brands have near-identical demographic and attitudinal profiles; exceptions are functionally different sub-markets. Core counter-evidence to 'brand-level' segmentation; supports positioning on distinctiveness and broad reach.
course_use: Critical reading for the STP critique session; pair with P&G 2016 example. Free repository copy.

title: Binet and Field: Media in Focus - Marketing Effectiveness in the Digital Era (IPA, 2017)
author_source: Les Binet, Peter Field; IPA, 2017; part 1 free via Thinkbox
note: Analysis of the IPA Databank asking whether tight targeting or mass marketing is more effective; finds share of voice still drives market share. Practitioner evidence for the targeting-vs-reach debate.
course_use: Supplementary reading for the critique session. Free (part 1).

title: Target pregnancy prediction - 'How Companies Learn Your Secrets'
author_source: Charles Duhigg, New York Times Magazine, 16/19 February 2012; paywalled article; critique by KDnuggets (Piatetsky, 2014)
note: Target statistician built a pregnancy-prediction score from about 25 products to target expectant mothers in the second trimester. The famous teenage-daughter anecdote is disputed (KDnuggets 2014). Teaches predictive targeting, life-event segments and privacy/creepiness limits.
course_use: Ethics discussion on predictive targeting; also discuss myth vs. evidence. NYT paywall (some free articles).

title: Psychological targeting as an effective approach to digital mass persuasion (PNAS 2017)
author_source: Sandra C. Matz, Michal Kosinski, Gideon Nave, David J. Stillwell; PNAS 114(48), 12714-12719; open access (PMC)
note: Field experiments with 3.5 million people: ads matched to personality (extraversion, openness) predicted from Facebook Likes produced up to 40% more clicks and 50% more purchases. Scientific basis for psychographic micro-targeting and the Cambridge Analytica debate; authors discuss manipulation risks.
course_use: Reading for ethics of psychographic targeting; quick in-class replication of persona-matched ads. Free.

title: Cambridge Analytica - ICO investigation into data analytics in political campaigns (2018)
author_source: UK Information Commissioner's Office report to Parliament, November 2018; summary by Society for Computers and Law; free
note: Largest data-protection investigation of its kind: micro-targeting of political ads, Facebook's failure to safeguard data, enforcement against SCL Elections and AggregateIQ. Defines the ethical and legal boundary of psychographic targeting.
course_use: Ethics/regulation session; pair with Matz et al. 2017. Free.

title: Meta lookalike audiences - how algorithmic targeting builds 'segments' from seed customers
author_source: Meta Business Help Centre, 'Lookalike Audiences'; free
note: Explains how advertisers upload a source audience (customers, pixel events) and Meta finds similar users. Shows how targeting has moved from marketer-defined segments to platform-modelled audiences; discuss transparency and GDPR.
course_use: Short demo in class (show Ads Manager screenshots); discussion on who now does the segmenting. Free.

title: Oesterreichische Post 'Parteiaffinitaet' - EUR 18m GDPR fine (2019) for a data-broker segmentation
author_source: netzpolitik.org, 29 October 2019; follow-ups in futurezone (fine later annulled on formal grounds; civil damages paid); free
note: Austrian Post computed estimated party affinity for about 2.2 million people by combining surveys, election results and statistics with name, address, gender and age, and marketed it for targeted election advertising; also used parcel and relocation data for direct marketing. Austrian case on the legal limits of segmentation data.
course_use: Austrian ethics/GDPR case for discussion or exam question. Free (German).

title: jö Bonus Club (Rewe Austria) - EUR 2m fine over profiling consent (2021)
author_source: futurezone.at, 3 August 2021; follow-up reporting on reduced data collection 2025 (Salzburg24); free
note: Austria's largest loyalty programme (more than 4 million members; Billa, Penny, Bipa and partners) profiled purchase data for personalised offers; the data protection authority found members were not adequately informed about profiling (data of 2.3 million people). Austrian counterpart to Tesco Clubcard for behavioural segmentation and its limits.
course_use: Austrian example: compare jö with Tesco Clubcard; discussion on consent-based targeting. Free (German).

title: Harrah's/Caesars Total Rewards - 'Diamonds in the Data Mine'
author_source: Gary Loveman, Harvard Business Review, May 2003 (reprint R0305H); approx. USD 9
note: Former HBS professor turned COO/CEO explains how database marketing and decision science identified the most valuable customer segments (low-to-mid-stakes locals) and drove loyalty incentives. Practitioner companion to the Harrah's case on value-based segmentation.
course_use: Reading alongside the Harrah's case. Paid (HBR); WU-Lizenz prüfen (EBSCO Business Source).

title: scikit-learn clustering module (KMeans, AgglomerativeClustering, GaussianMixture, DBSCAN, HDBSCAN)
author_source: scikit-learn developers, PyPI, v1.9.1, BSD-3-Clause, 2026, Python library
note: Core Python toolkit for the S in STP: KMeans (k-means++ init), AgglomerativeClustering (Ward linkage; dendrogram via scipy), GaussianMixture (BIC for number of segments, soft membership), DBSCAN and sklearn.cluster.HDBSCAN (since 1.3) for outliers/niche segments; silhouette_score and calinski_harabasz_score; StandardScaler for preprocessing. Lets students compare partitioning, hierarchical and model-based segmentation on the same data.
course_use: Main engine for Python-track labs (Mall Customers, Wholesale, RFM data); free, pip/conda, runs in Google Colab without setup.

title: scikit-learn MDS and PCA for perceptual maps (sklearn.manifold.MDS, sklearn.decomposition.PCA)
author_source: scikit-learn developers, PyPI, v1.9.1, BSD-3-Clause, 2026, Python library
note: MDS (metric/non-metric, dissimilarity='precomputed') turns brand dissimilarity matrices into 2-D perceptual maps; PCA on mean brand x attribute ratings yields attribute-based positioning biplots - the Python counterpart to Chapman & Feit ch. 8.
course_use: Positioning lab: perceptual map from brand.ratings or own class survey; free.

title: kmodes (k-modes and k-prototypes clustering)
author_source: Nico de Vos, PyPI/GitHub, v0.12.2, MIT, Python library
note: KModes clusters purely categorical survey data (demographics, yes/no items); KPrototypes handles mixed numeric + categorical bases (e.g. Customer Personality Analysis: income + education + marital status). cost_ attribute for elbow plots. Shows why k-means on dummy codes is problematic.
course_use: Lab extension for mixed-type segmentation bases; free, pip install kmodes.

title: StepMix (latent class / latent profile analysis with covariates)
author_source: Morin, Legault, Laliberté et al., PyPI/GitHub, v3.0.0, MIT, Python library (R wrapper available)
note: Scikit-learn-style API for latent class (categorical items) and latent profile (continuous) models with 1-, 2- and 3-step (BCH, ML) estimation of segment-covariate relations and distal outcomes; BIC/entropy for model selection. Best Python option to teach model-based segmentation (Wedel & Kamakura tradition).
course_use: Master-level lab: LCA on survey items, then describe segments with demographics; free.

title: yellowbrick cluster visualizers (KElbowVisualizer, SilhouetteVisualizer, InterclusterDistance)
author_source: District Data Labs, PyPI, v1.5, Apache-2.0, last release 2022, Python library
note: One-line diagnostics for choosing the number of segments: elbow with automatic knee (distortion/silhouette/calinski_harabasz), per-cluster silhouette plot, intercluster distance map. No release since 2022 - test compatibility with current scikit-learn before class.
course_use: Lab step 'how many segments?'; free, pip install yellowbrick.

title: prince (PCA, CA, MCA, FAMD, MFA in Python)
author_source: Max Halford, PyPI/GitHub, v0.21.0, MIT, Python library
note: Correspondence analysis on brand x attribute association counts and MCA on categorical survey data, with row/column coordinate plots - the standard way to build attribute-based perceptual maps from pick-any brand-image data; FAMD as preprocessing for mixed data before clustering.
course_use: Positioning lab in Python (CA perceptual map); free.

title: umap-learn (UMAP dimensionality reduction)
author_source: Leland McInnes et al., PyPI, v0.5.12, BSD-3-Clause, Python library
note: Non-linear 2-D projection to visualise segment structure in high-dimensional behavioural data (e.g. Instacart department-share vectors); often paired with HDBSCAN. Good for contrasting with PCA and warning that visual clumps are not yet actionable segments.
course_use: Demo / advanced project; free.

title: PyMC-Marketing (CLV module: BG/NBD, Pareto/NBD, Gamma-Gamma; RFM summary)
author_source: PyMC Labs, PyPI/GitHub, v1.2.0, Apache-2.0, Python library
note: Bayesian successor to lifetimes: clv.utils.rfm_summary builds frequency/recency/T/monetary from transaction logs; BetaGeoModel, ParetoNBDModel and GammaGammaModel predict purchases and CLV per customer - supports value-based targeting (which segments to acquire/retain). Also contains media mix models.
course_use: Targeting lab on Online Retail II or CDNOW: RFM, fit BG/NBD, rank customers by CLV; free.

title: lifetimes (classic CLV / RFM models)
author_source: Cameron Davidson-Pilon, PyPI/GitHub, v0.11.3, MIT, last release 2020 (unmaintained), Python library
note: summary_data_from_transaction_data, BetaGeoFitter, GammaGammaFitter, probability-alive matrices. Used in most Kaggle RFM/CLV notebooks, but unmaintained since 2020 - recommend PyMC-Marketing for new material.
course_use: Reading/adapting existing notebooks; free.

title: scikit-uplift (sklift)
author_source: maks-sh et al., PyPI/GitHub, v0.5.1, MIT, 2022, Python library
note: Uplift (incremental response) modelling for targeting: S-learner, T-learner, class transformation; uplift_at_k, Qini and uplift curves; built-in datasets (fetch_hillstrom, fetch_x5, fetch_criteo, fetch_megafon). Teaches that the best target is the persuadable, not the likely buyer.
course_use: Targeting lab with the Hillstrom e-mail data; free.

title: CausalML (uplift and heterogeneous treatment effects)
author_source: Uber Technologies, PyPI/GitHub, v0.18.0, Apache-2.0, Python library
note: Meta-learners (S/T/X/R) plus uplift trees/forests; feature importance of uplift drivers helps describe persuadable segments. More research-grade than sklift.
course_use: Master-level targeting project; free.

title: hdbscan (standalone library)
author_source: McInnes, Healy et al. (scikit-learn-contrib), PyPI, v0.8.44, BSD-3-Clause, Python library
note: Density-based hierarchical clustering with soft membership, outlier scores and condensed-tree plots; finds niche segments without fixing k. Adds richer diagnostics than sklearn's built-in HDBSCAN.
course_use: Optional advanced lab; free.

title: pandas RFM segmentation recipe (groupby + qcut)
author_source: pandas development team, PyPI, BSD-3-Clause, Python library
note: Transparent RFM without modelling: groupby(customer).agg(recency, frequency = nunique invoices, monetary = sum), pd.qcut into quintiles, concatenate scores and map to named segments (Champions, Loyal, At Risk, Hibernating). Ideal first coding exercise before clustering.
course_use: Intro lab on UCI Online Retail II; free.

title: flexclust (flexible cluster algorithms, segment stability)
author_source: Friedrich Leisch, CRAN, v1.5.0, GPL-2, 2025, R package
note: Engine behind the Dolnicar/Grün/Leisch segmentation approach: stepFlexclust (repeated k-means over k), bootFlexclust and slswFlexclust for global and segment-level stability, barchart() segment profile plots, segment separation plots; ships datasets vacmot, ausActiv, winterActiv.
course_use: Core R lab following steps 5-7 of 'Market Segmentation Analysis'; free.

title: MSA - companion R package to 'Market Segmentation Analysis' (Dolnicar, Grün & Leisch 2018)
author_source: Leisch, Grün & Dolnicar, BOKU Vienna website (not on CRAN), v0.3-1, source tarball, R package
note: Contains all datasets of the open-access Springer book (mcdonalds, Australian travel motives, vacation activities, Austrian winter activities, risk taking) and every analysis as demo('step-4') ... demo('step-9'). Austrian authors (BOKU, JKU) give a local connection for WU students.
course_use: Ready-made 10-step segmentation lab with book chapters as reading; free, install.packages(<tarball URL>, repos=NULL, type='source').

title: poLCA (polytomous variable latent class analysis)
author_source: Drew Linzer & Jeffrey Lewis, CRAN, v1.6.0.2, GPL (>=2), 2026, R package
note: Latent class segmentation of categorical survey items, latent class regression with covariates, AIC/BIC for number of classes; classic for attitudinal and lifestyle segmentation (e.g. ESS values items).
course_use: R lab on model-based segmentation; free.

title: mclust (Gaussian mixture model clustering)
author_source: Scrucca, Fraley, Murphy & Raftery, CRAN, v6.1.3, GPL (>=2), 2026, R package
note: Model-based clustering with automatic choice of covariance structure and number of segments by BIC (plot(Mclust(x), 'BIC')); per-customer classification uncertainty for discussing fuzzy segment membership. Used in Chapman & Feit ch. 11.
course_use: R lab, comparison with k-means; free.

title: cluster (methods from Kaufman & Rousseeuw 'Finding Groups in Data')
author_source: Maechler, Rousseeuw, Struyf, Hubert, Hornik, CRAN, v2.1.8.3, GPL (>=2), 2026, R recommended package
note: pam (k-medoids, robust to outliers), clara (large n), agnes/diana (hierarchical), daisy (Gower distance for mixed survey data), silhouette(). Gower + PAM is the standard answer for mixed-type segmentation bases.
course_use: Standard R lab tool; free, ships with R.

title: factoextra (visualising clustering and multivariate results)
author_source: Alboukadel Kassambara & Fabian Mundt, CRAN, v2.2.0, GPL-2, 2026, R package
note: ggplot2-based fviz_nbclust (elbow, silhouette, gap statistic), fviz_cluster (segments on PC axes), fviz_dend, fviz_ca_biplot for CA perceptual maps. Slide-ready plots with minimal code.
course_use: R labs for both segmentation and positioning; free.

title: FactoMineR (PCA, CA, MCA, HCPC)
author_source: Husson, Josse, Lê, Mazet, CRAN, v2.18, GPL (>=2), 2026, R package
note: CA() for brand x attribute perceptual maps, MCA() for categorical surveys, HCPC() for hierarchical clustering on principal components with automatic segment description (v.test of descriptor variables) - positioning and segment profiling in one package; Factoshiny adds a point-and-click interface.
course_use: Positioning lab (CA map) and segment profiling; free.

title: smacof (multidimensional scaling and unfolding)
author_source: Patrick Mair, Jan de Leeuw, Patrick Groenen, CRAN, v2.1-7, GPL-3, 2024, R package

course_use: Advanced positioning lab; free.

title: NbClust (determining the number of clusters)
author_source: Charrad, Ghazzali, Boiteau, Niknafs, CRAN, v3.0.1, GPL-2, 2022, R package
note: Computes up to 30 indices and a majority vote for k; good discussion starter that 'optimal k' is not unique and must be judged with managerial knock-out criteria (Dolnicar et al.).
course_use: Lab step on segment number; free.

title: tidyclust (tidymodels interface to clustering)
author_source: Emil Hvitfeldt, Kelly Bodwin et al., CRAN, v0.3.2, MIT, 2026, R package
note: k_means() and hier_clust() specifications inside tidymodels recipes/workflows, tune_cluster() for k, extract_centroids(); consistent with tidyverse-based teaching.
course_use: R labs for tidyverse-trained students; free.

title: flexmix (finite mixtures of regression models)
author_source: Bettina Grün & Friedrich Leisch, CRAN, v2.3-21, GPL (>=2), 2026, R package
note: Response-based segmentation: segments differing in price sensitivity or attribute importance (mixture regressions, latent-class conjoint); used in the MSA book for model-based segmentation.
course_use: Master/advanced lab; free.

title: depmixS4 (hidden Markov / dependent mixture models)
author_source: Ingmar Visser & Maarten Speekenbrink, CRAN, GPL (>=2), R package
note: Dynamic segmentation: customers switch between latent states (active, dormant, lapsed) over time; extends static STP to state-based customer journey models.
course_use: Research-level demo only; free.

title: Orange Data Mining (visual clustering workflows)
author_source: University of Ljubljana Bioinformatics Lab, v3.40.0, GPL-3, desktop GUI built on Python
note: Drag-and-drop widgets: File > Preprocess > k-Means (silhouette shown per k) / Hierarchical Clustering / DBSCAN > Box Plot, Scatter Plot, Silhouette Plot; MDS, t-SNE and Correspondence Analysis widgets for maps. Students build a full segmentation pipeline without code; many free video tutorials.

title: jamovi with snowCluster module

course_use: GUI lab for an SPSS-like workflow; free.

title: JASP Machine Learning module (clustering)
author_source: University of Amsterdam, JASP, AGPL-3, desktop GUI

course_use: GUI lab; free.

title: IBM SPSS Statistics TwoStep Cluster
author_source: IBM, commercial desktop software
note: TwoStep handles mixed categorical/continuous variables and suggests k via BIC; Model Viewer shows predictor importance and cluster profiles - still common in practitioner market research and textbooks (e.g. Sarstedt & Mooi).
course_use: Demo where a campus licence exists; paid.

title: KNIME Analytics Platform
author_source: KNIME AG, GPL-3 (with exceptions), desktop GUI

title: Hillstrom MineThatData E-Mail Analytics challenge
author_source: Kevin Hillstrom, MineThatData blog 2008; also sklift.datasets.fetch_hillstrom
note: 64,000 customers randomised to men's e-mail, women's e-mail or no e-mail; recency, history, mens/womens purchases, zip_code type, newbie, channel; outcomes visit, conversion, spend. The canonical dataset for uplift-based targeting and segment-level response.
course_use: Targeting lab with scikit-uplift; free.

title: CDNOW customer transactions (Fader & Hardie)
author_source: Peter Fader & Bruce Hardie, brucehardie.com, free for teaching
note: 23,570 customers who first bought at CDNOW in Q1 1997, tracked to mid-1998 (date, quantity, spend). Benchmark for BG/NBD and Pareto/NBD CLV models used in PyMC-Marketing and lifetimes examples - value-based targeting.
course_use: CLV targeting lab; free.

title: European Social Survey (ESS)
author_source: ESS ERIC, free for non-commercial use with registration, biennial since 2002
note: Cross-national survey (~30 countries incl. Austria) with the 21-item Schwartz human values scale, media use, trust, social and political attitudes, demographics. Excellent for values-based psychographic segmentation of Austrian/European consumers.
course_use: Project data for attitudinal segmentation (poLCA/StepMix); free with registration.

title: World Values Survey (Wave 7) and joint EVS/WVS
author_source: World Values Survey Association, free for non-commercial use with registration
note: Values and beliefs in ~90 countries; the Inglehart-Welzel cultural map is itself a positioning map of countries - good for international segmentation and country clustering.
course_use: International segmentation project; free, registration.

title: Eurobarometer microdata via GESIS
author_source: European Commission; archived at GESIS Data Archive, free for academic use with registration
note: Standard and Special Eurobarometer surveys with modules on consumer attitudes, sustainability, digital behaviour and food; individual microdata for segmenting EU consumers (e.g. green consumer segments) across countries.
course_use: Project data; free with GESIS login.

title: Social Survey Austria (SSÖ) and other Austrian surveys via AUSSDA
author_source: AUSSDA - The Austrian Social Science Data Archive (Dataverse), registration, scientific use
note: Social Survey Austria waves (since 1986) on values, leisure, work and inequality, plus Values in Crisis, AUTNES and others. Local microdata for lifestyle segmentation exercises.
course_use: Austrian project data; free for academic users with login.

title: GESIS ALLBUS (German General Social Survey)
author_source: GESIS, free for academic use with registration
note: Biennial German survey with values, media use, consumption-related attitudes and demographics; ALLBUS compact versions are manageable for students; DACH comparison to Austrian data.
course_use: Project data; free with login.

title: Statistik Austria Konsumerhebung (household budget survey)
author_source: Statistik Austria, published tables free; microdata via Austrian Micro Data Center
note: Five-yearly survey of Austrian household expenditure by COICOP category, broken down by household type, income decile and region - estimate segment market size as spend per household x households in segment.
course_use: Market-sizing exercise for segment attractiveness; tables free.

title: STATcube and Statistik Austria open data (population, households, tourism)
author_source: Statistik Austria, STATcube free basic access, OGD under CC BY 4.0
note: Population by age, sex, Bundesland/district, households by type, income and tourism nights by origin market - the denominators for segment size and potential (e.g. single households aged 25-34 in Vienna).
course_use: Segment sizing assignment; free.

title: Eurostat database (Household Budget Survey, demography, ICT usage by individuals)
author_source: Eurostat, free reuse with attribution
note: HBS expenditure structure, population statistics and 'ICT usage in households and by individuals' (e.g. online shopping by age and education) for cross-country segment sizing and selecting target countries.
course_use: International targeting and market sizing exercise; free.

title: data.gv.at and data.europa.eu open data portals
author_source: Austrian Federal Chancellery; Publications Office of the EU
note: Catalogues of open public datasets (e.g. City of Vienna district statistics, tourism arrivals by country of origin) for geographic segmentation and local market sizing; data.europa.eu covers EU-wide portals.
course_use: Student project data search; free.

title: Zenodo and Harvard Dataverse segmentation replication data
author_source: Zenodo (CERN), Harvard Dataverse; licences per dataset (often CC BY)
note: Replication data from published segmentation studies (tourism, food, energy, mobility consumers): real survey data with a reference solution to compare students' segments against.
course_use: Replication project for Master students; free.

title: Thomas Reutterer
author_source: WU Vienna, Professor of Marketing and Head of the Institute for Marketing and Customer Analytics; Wien; academic
note: Customer-base analysis, CRM, probabilistic models of customer behaviour, data-driven segmentation of retail customers; ISMS Practice Prize finalist; publications in JMR and Marketing Science; founding academic director of the WU MSc Marketing. Presents in German and English.
course_use: Ideal on-site guest lecture (same campus) on behavioural/CLV-based segmentation vs. survey-based segmentation and how retailers target with loyalty data; also fits a methods Q&A. Contact via institute page.

title: Martin Schreier
author_source: WU Vienna, Professor of Marketing, Head of the Department of Marketing and the Institute for Marketing Management; Wien; academic
note: Product and brand management, consumer behaviour, user-driven innovation; former Editor-in-Chief of IJRM (EMAC journal, 2021-2024), EMAC Fellow since 2024; MSI expert directory member. Relevant for positioning (e.g. 'user-designed' product labels as a positioning cue). German/English.
course_use: On-site session on brand positioning and consumer-perception experiments; good for linking STP to current consumer research. Contact via institute page.

title: Nils Wlömert
author_source: WU Vienna, Professor of Marketing and Head of the Institute for Retailing & Data Science (RDS); Wien; academic
note: Quantitative marketing, retail analytics, platform economics, music streaming (IJRM Best Paper 2016 on Spotify market entry). Teaches data-science-oriented retail marketing (SBWL Handel & Marketing). German/English.
course_use: On-site guest input on data-driven targeting in retail and platforms, or a hands-on R/Python segmentation exercise. Contact via institute page.

title: Bodo B. Schlegelmilch
author_source: WU Vienna, Professor of International Marketing and Management (Institute for International Marketing Management; verify current/emeritus status); Wien; academic
note: Author of 'Global Marketing Strategy' (Springer) covering international market segmentation and cross-country positioning; long-standing WU Executive Academy dean. English/German.
course_use: Possible on-site lecture on international segmentation (country vs. cross-national consumer segments). Verify availability via institute.

title: Bertram Barth
author_source: INTEGRAL Markt- und Meinungsforschung, Vienna, long-serving managing director (current role to verify; INTEGRAL now part of INTEGRAL-SINUS-OPINION group); Wien; practitioner
note: Driving figure behind the Sinus-Milieus Austria (10 value- and lifestyle-based milieus) and INTEGRAL's 2009 majority stake in SINUS Heidelberg; frequent speaker on milieu-based segmentation. German.
course_use: Strong practitioner guest (on site in Vienna) for psychographic/lifestyle segmentation; alternatively invite current INTEGRAL management (e.g. Martin Mayr). Contact via company website.

title: Martin Mayr
author_source: INTEGRAL Markt- und Meinungsforschung, Vienna, managing director (Geschäftsführung, with background in financial services and advanced analytics); Wien; practitioner
note: Co-leads INTEGRAL, licence holder of the Sinus-Milieus in Austria; 2025 partnership with YouGov CP Austria brought Sinus-Milieus into the YouGov Shopper Panel (from Nov 2025) - a current example of milieu-based targeting of shoppers. German.
course_use: On-site talk on how brands and media use Sinus-Milieus for targeting and media planning. Contact via company website.

title: Thomas (Tommy) Schwabl
author_source: Marketagent (online market research, panel), Baden bei Wien, founder and managing director; Österreich; practitioner
note: Founded Marketagent in 2000, one of Austria's leading online research institutes with a large consumer panel; regular public studies and 'Research on Research'; launched AI interview tool Glaut in Austria. Source of Austrian consumer-segment studies. German.
course_use: Good practitioner guest (on site, near Vienna) on survey-based segmentation in practice, panels and AI-assisted research. Contact via company website.

title: Bettina Grün
author_source: Department of Statistics, Universität Innsbruck (her personal homepage now redirects there; previously Institute for Statistics and Mathematics, WU Vienna - verify current position); Österreich; academic
note: Co-author (with Sara Dolnicar and the late Friedrich Leisch, BOKU, d. 2024) of the open-access book 'Market Segmentation Analysis' (Springer 2018) with R code; co-author of R packages flexmix and flexclust (model-based and partitioning clustering) and the MSA package; Charles R. Goeldner Article of Excellence Award. English/German.
course_use: Excellent methods guest (remote or on site) for the data-driven segmentation step: cluster analysis, segment stability, R demo with the book's datasets. Contact via university page.

title: Sara Dolnicar
author_source: University of Queensland, Professor (Research Professor of Tourism, UQ Business School); Global (Austrian-born, WU Vienna alumna); academic
note: Leading voice on market segmentation methodology; lead author of 'Market Segmentation Analysis' (open access, Springer 2018) and of an edX MOOC on segmentation; 300+ refereed papers, ARC Laureate Fellow. Presented on Leisch's segmentation contributions at the 2025 BOKU memorial symposium. English/German.
course_use: Remote guest lecture or recorded interview on the 10-step segmentation process and common segmentation pitfalls; time zone (Brisbane) needs early-morning or evening slot.

title: Michel Wedel
author_source: University of Maryland, Robert H. Smith School of Business, Distinguished University Professor (PepsiCo Chair in Consumer Science); Global; academic
note: Co-author with Wagner Kamakura of 'Market Segmentation: Conceptual and Methodological Foundations' (Kluwer/Springer), the standard reference on latent-class/mixture segmentation; also visual marketing and eye tracking. English.
course_use: Primarily a reading-list author; remote Q&A possible for a master's-level methods session.

title: Wagner A. Kamakura
author_source: Rice University, Jones Graduate School of Business, Professor Emeritus of Marketing (verify); Global; academic
note: Co-author of 'Market Segmentation: Conceptual and Methodological Foundations' with Michel Wedel; work on latent-class segmentation, cross-selling and database marketing. English/Portuguese.
course_use: Reading-list author; recorded talks rather than live guest lecture.

title: Catherine Tucker
author_source: MIT Sloan School of Management, Sloan Distinguished Professor of Management and Professor of Marketing; Global; academic
note: Research on online advertising, ad targeting and privacy: the trade-off between targeting precision and privacy intrusion, effects of privacy regulation on ad effectiveness, field experiments on privacy choices. Directly relevant to the ethics and regulation of targeting (GDPR context). English.
course_use: Use her papers and MIT IDE podcast/video talks in the targeting and ethics session; remote guest unlikely but recorded material is plentiful.

title: Oded Netzer
author_source: Columbia Business School, Arthur J. Samberg Professor of Business; Global; academic
note: Text mining for marketing: building perceptual/positioning maps from online text and forum data ('Mine Your Own Business', Marketing Science 2012); customer-base analytics. Shows modern data sources for positioning analysis. English.
course_use: Recorded talks or remote Q&A on data-driven perceptual maps; papers for advanced readings.

title: Gary L. Lilien
author_source: Penn State Smeal College of Business, Distinguished Research Professor Emeritus of Management Science; co-founder of DecisionPro; Global; academic
note: Co-author with Arvind Rangaswamy (and Kristin Grimm) of 'Principles of Marketing Engineering and Analytics' with Enginius software covering segmentation, targeting and positioning models (cluster analysis, perceptual maps); ISMS Practice Prize founder. English.
course_use: Reading-list and software author; the Enginius/Marketing Engineering cases fit STP workshop sessions.

note: Co-author with Chris Chapman of 'R for Marketing Research and Analytics' (Springer Use R!, 2nd ed. 2019; Python edition 2023) incl. chapter 'Segmentation: Clustering and Classification' with open code; experiments and marketing analytics. English.
course_use: Remote guest or her free online materials/workshops for a hands-on segmentation lab in R or Python.

title: Chris Chapman
author_source: Quantitative UX researcher (formerly Google, Microsoft, Amazon; verify current affiliation); co-founder of the Quant UX Association; Global; practitioner/communicator
note: Co-author of 'R for Marketing Research and Analytics' and 'Python for Marketing Research and Analytics'; practitioner of segmentation, conjoint and MaxDiff in tech product research. English.

title: Philip Kotler
author_source: Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University, S.C. Johnson Distinguished Professor Emeritus of International Marketing; Global; academic/communicator
note: Popularised the STP framework through 'Marketing Management' (with Kevin Lane Keller) and 'Principles of Marketing'; many keynote recordings. English.
course_use: Not realistic as live guest; use recorded keynotes/interviews to introduce STP as canonical framework.

title: Kevin Lane Keller
author_source: Tuck School of Business at Dartmouth, E.B. Osborn Professor of Marketing; Global; academic
note: Co-author of 'Marketing Management' and author of 'Strategic Brand Management'; customer-based brand equity, points of parity and points of difference as the core of positioning statements. English.
course_use: Reading-list author; recorded lectures on brand positioning (POP/POD).

title: Byron Sharp
author_source: Ehrenberg-Bass Institute for Marketing Science, University of South Australia, Director and Professor of Marketing Science; Global; academic/communicator
note: Author of 'How Brands Grow'; argues for broad reach and mental/physical availability rather than tight targeting and differentiation (distinctiveness over differentiation) - the key counter-position to classic STP. English.
course_use: Remote talk or recorded debate material; pair with Ritson for a 'targeting vs. mass marketing' discussion.

title: Jenni Romaniuk
author_source: Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, University of South Australia, Research Professor and Associate Director (International); Global; academic
note: Author of 'Building Distinctive Brand Assets' and 'Better Brand Health', co-author of 'How Brands Grow Part 2'; category entry points as an alternative lens on targeting and positioning. English.
course_use: Remote guest or webinar recordings on category entry points and distinctiveness.

title: Malcolm McDonald
author_source: Cranfield School of Management, Emeritus Professor of Marketing; Global; academic
note: Co-author with Ian Dunbar of 'Market Segmentation: How to Do It and How to Profit from It' and author of 'Marketing Plans'; practitioner-oriented needs-based segmentation process. English.
course_use: Reading-list author for the managerial segmentation process; recorded material only.

title: Sally Dibb
author_source: Coventry University, Professor of Marketing and Society (verify current affiliation); Global; academic
note: With Lyndon Simkin author of 'Market Segmentation Success: Making It Happen!' and the 'Marketing Planning' workbooks; research on segmentation implementation barriers. English.
course_use: Remote guest on why segmentation projects fail in implementation; articles for advanced readings.

title: Lyndon Simkin
author_source: Coventry University, Professor of Strategic Marketing (verify current affiliation); Global; academic
note: Co-author with Sally Dibb of segmentation and marketing-planning texts; research on segmentation implementation and diagnosing segmentation problems. English.
course_use: Remote guest or recorded talk paired with Dibb.

title: Mark Ritson
author_source: Marketing Week columnist and founder of the Mini MBA in Marketing and Mini MBA in Brand Management; former professor (MBS, Minnesota, LBS); Global; communicator
note: Strong advocate of rigorous diagnosis-strategy-tactics with explicit segmentation, targeting and positioning; columns and videos debating Byron Sharp's anti-targeting stance. English.
course_use: Use columns and YouTube videos as discussion starters; live guest unlikely but his Mini MBA material maps directly onto STP.

title: April Dunford
author_source: Positioning consultant for B2B tech companies; author of 'Obviously Awesome' and 'Sales Pitch'; Global; practitioner/communicator
note: Step-by-step positioning method (competitive alternatives, unique attributes, value, best-fit customers, market category); offers consulting, keynotes, templates, a Substack newsletter and the podcast 'The Positioning Show'. English.
course_use: Remote keynote or recorded talks; her free templates work well for a student positioning workshop.

title: Les Binet
author_source: adam&eveDDB, Group Head of Effectiveness; Global; practitioner
note: Co-author with Peter Field of 'The Long and the Short of It' (IPA) using the IPA Databank; evidence on broad reach vs. targeted activation (60/40 rule), relevant to targeting breadth decisions. English.
course_use: Recorded IPA/conference talks; remote Q&A possible via IPA network.

title: Peter Field
author_source: Independent marketing effectiveness consultant; co-author with Les Binet of IPA effectiveness studies; Global; practitioner
note: IPA Databank analyses ('The Long and the Short of It', 'Media in Focus', 'The Crisis in Creative Effectiveness') informing how wide to target and how to balance brand and activation. English.
course_use: Recorded talks; remote guest possible.

title: Laura Ries
author_source: Ries & Ries (Atlanta), President; Global; practitioner/communicator
note: Co-author with her late father Al Ries (d. 2022) of positioning and branding books ('The 22 Immutable Laws of Branding', 'Visual Hammer', 'Battlecry'); continues the Ries & Trout positioning tradition (Jack Trout d. 2017). English.
course_use: Recorded talks/podcast appearances to illustrate classic positioning theory ('owning a word in the mind').

title: Renée Mauborgne
author_source: INSEAD, Professor of Strategy and co-director of the INSEAD Blue Ocean Strategy Institute; Global; academic
note: With W. Chan Kim author of 'Blue Ocean Strategy' and 'Blue Ocean Shift'; strategy canvas and non-customer tiers as a tool for repositioning and targeting non-customers. English.
course_use: Recorded talks; strategy-canvas exercise as alternative to perceptual maps.

title: Bob Moesta
author_source: The Re-Wired Group (Detroit), CEO and founder; research fellow at the Christensen Institute; Global; practitioner
note: Co-architect with the late Clayton Christensen (d. 2020) of Jobs-to-be-Done theory; author of 'Demand-Side Sales 101'; switch interviews and forces of progress as a needs-based alternative to demographic segmentation. English.
course_use: Remote guest or podcast/video material for a session on needs-/jobs-based segmentation.

title: Franz-Rudolf Esch
author_source: EBS Universität für Wirtschaft und Recht, Professor of Brand Management and Automotive Marketing; founder of ESCH. The Brand Consultants; Global (DACH); academic/practitioner
note: Author of 'Strategie und Technik der Markenführung' (German standard text) with brand positioning models (e.g. Markensteuerrad). German.
course_use: German-language reading; remote guest possible for brand positioning session.

title: Christian Homburg
author_source: University of Mannheim, Professor of Business Administration and Marketing; chairman of Homburg & Partner (now part of Simon-Kucher; verify); Global (DACH); academic/practitioner
note: Author of 'Marketingmanagement' (German standard textbook with segmentation and positioning chapters); B2B and customer-management research. German/English.
course_use: German textbook reference; remote guest possible.

title: Manfred Kirchgeorg
author_source: HHL Leipzig Graduate School of Management, Professor (SVI-Endowed Chair of Marketing Management and Sustainability); Global (DACH); academic
note: Co-author with Heribert Meffert et al. of 'Marketing: Grundlagen marktorientierter Unternehmensführung', the classic German text with market segmentation and positioning chapters. German.
course_use: German textbook reference; remote guest possible.

title: EMAC - European Marketing Academy
author_source: EMAC; academic association; Europe; annual conference (May/June) plus regional conferences and doctoral colloquia
note: Main European academic marketing community; publishes IJRM; many segmentation, targeting and positioning papers in conference proceedings. WU Vienna faculty strongly represented.
course_use: Students can follow proceedings and IJRM; membership and conference fees apply (reduced for doctoral students).

title: AMA - American Marketing Association
author_source: AMA; professional and academic association; Global (US-based); Winter and Summer Academic Conferences, practitioner events, webinars
note: Publishes Journal of Marketing and JMR; Marketing News and free articles on segmentation, positioning and targeting; AMA definitions frequently cited.
course_use: Free articles online; student membership available for a fee.

title: ISMS Marketing Science Conference
author_source: INFORMS Society for Marketing Science; academic conference; Global (rotating location); annual (June)
note: Leading quantitative marketing conference with sessions on segmentation, targeting algorithms, personalisation and privacy; ISMS Practice Prize showcases applied work (WU's Reutterer team was a finalist).
course_use: Mainly for master's/PhD students; practice-prize videos and papers are useful course materials.

title: Marketing Science Institute (MSI) incl. Research Priorities
author_source: MSI; industry-academic research institute; Global (US); research priorities updated periodically (2024 priorities current), annual Summit, research calls
note: 2024 research priorities cover Marketing Analytics (AI, models, measurement), Consumer Experiences, Stakeholders and Innovation, including privacy-driven changes to targeting and fragmented customer journeys; working papers and webinars. Martin Schreier listed in MSI expert directory.
course_use: Use the priorities document to frame thesis topics on STP; some working papers free, full access via member firms.

title: ESOMAR
author_source: ESOMAR; global market-research association; Amsterdam/Global; annual Congress, webinars, guidelines
note: Codes and guidelines on research ethics and data protection relevant to segmentation surveys and targeting; Research World magazine; global market research market statistics.
course_use: Free young-professional/student resources; full membership paid.

title: VMÖ - Verband der Marktforscher Österreichs
author_source: VMÖ; Austrian market research association; Österreich (Wien); events and professional standards
note: Network of Austrian market research institutes (e.g. INTEGRAL, Marketagent, Spectra, Gallup Austria) - source for local segmentation practitioners and guest speakers.
course_use: Check events for open sessions; good starting point for recruiting Austrian research guest speakers.

title: IPA Effectiveness Awards and IPA Databank
author_source: IPA (Institute of Practitioners in Advertising); UK industry association; London/Global; biennial awards, ongoing databank publications
note: Award-winning case studies document how campaigns defined target audiences and positioning and the commercial results; basis of Binet and Field's effectiveness research.
course_use: Some case summaries and reports free, full databank access paid/member-only.

title: Marketing Week Mini MBA in Marketing
author_source: Marketing Week / Mark Ritson; online professional course; Global (online); cohorts several times a year
note: 12-week online course by Mark Ritson structured around diagnosis (research, segmentation), strategy (targeting, positioning, objectives) and tactics; large alumni community.
course_use: Paid course (not for students as course requirement); free marketing-week columns and preview videos usable in class.

title: Ehrenberg-Bass Institute Corporate Sponsors Programme
author_source: Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, University of South Australia; industry-academic sponsorship programme; Global (Adelaide); ongoing, sponsor reports and events
note: Sponsor companies receive evidence-based reports on brand growth, mental availability, category entry points and the limits of targeting; public outputs include books and articles.
course_use: Sponsorship is corporate-only; students can use public books and articles. Good contrast to classic STP.

title: Österreichische Marketing-Gesellschaft (ÖMG)
author_source: ÖMG; Austrian marketing association; Wien; Neujahrsempfang (January), Sommerfest (late August), 'ÖMG-Sandbox' think-tank format, Christmas event
note: Austria's marketing practitioner network; 2026 publication 'Marketing Utopias 2030 ff.' from the Sandbox format; awards for graduates with Werbe Akademie - networking with Austrian brand managers for STP guest speakers.
course_use: Students can attend selected events; membership with reduced rates for young professionals (verify).

title: Dialog Marketing Verband Österreich (DMVÖ)
author_source: DMVÖ; Austrian dialogue/data-driven marketing association; Wien; Sommerfest with 'Dialogmarketing Rookie of the Year' (Sept), journal 'Im Dialog' with FH St. Pölten
note: Community for CRM, data-driven targeting and direct marketing in Austria; publishes 'Im Dialog'; operates the young community Marketing Natives.
course_use: Students can join via Marketing Natives or student membership (verify cost); events in Vienna.

title: Marketing Natives
author_source: Young marketers' community powered by DMVÖ; Wien (also Zurich chapter); signature events several times a year (e.g. 26 May 2026 at Österreichische Post AG)
note: Events with marketing CEOs and brand leads on brand strategy and targeting in an algorithmic world (2026 event: 'Mehr als Algorithmen: Was Marken heute wirklich brauchen').
course_use: Free or low-cost for students and young professionals; good networking for internship and guest speaker contacts.

title: IAA Austrian Chapter and Effie Awards Austria
author_source: International Advertising Association Austria; industry association; Wien; Effie Austria annually (entries May-July, gala 12 Nov 2026)
note: Effie Austria rewards effective campaigns; 2026 shortlist of 79 campaigns in 20 categories; case summaries document target audiences, positioning and results of Austrian brands.
course_use: Use Effie case summaries as local STP cases; gala tickets paid, case material often public.

title: Vienna Data Science Group (VDSG)
author_source: VDSG; non-profit data science association; Wien; meetups and talks (venues incl. TU Wien), co-organiser of Women in Data Science Vienna
note: Practitioner talks on clustering, customer analytics and ML for marketing; network to find Vienna data scientists who do segmentation in industry.
course_use: Free meetups, open to students; join via website/Meetup.
